title: AI Research Scientist
descriptionHtml:
About the Science and AI Team

The Science and AI team is at the heart of Maki People. It builds the science and AI behind our platform, from job analysis and assessments to AI interviews and predicting performance. Led by our Head of Science, Aiden Loe, and working closely with our COO, Paul-Louis Caylar, the team brings together business psychologists, psychometricians and AI scientists. Together, they make sure every hiring decision on our platform is accurate, consistent and fair.

As Maki grows, the Science and AI team’s job is to show, with evidence, that our approach leads to better hiring decisions.

About the Role

The AI Research Scientist works at the intersection of AI, psychometrics and research, ensuring that Maki’s automated scoring systems are scientifically robust, fair, and continuously improving.

1. Evaluating and testing LLMs for scoring

  • Assess the accuracy and reliability of LLMs used for automated scoring, such as structured grids, job-specific skills and multilingual proficiency (written and spoken).

  • Benchmark closed- and open-source models across assessment types and languages.

  • Test robustness to prompt variation, input noise and adversarial behaviour such as prompt injection.

  • Explore prompt engineering and model optimisation, and recommend which models and prompts go into production.

2. Building our own scoring models

  • Move our scoring onto self-hosted open-weight models, and fine-tune them on expert-rated data where they can beat frontier models.

  • Check every model switch keeps accuracy, reliability and fairness at least as good as today's.

3. Comparing AI with human judgement, and calibrating psychometric models

  • Design studies that compare AI scores with expert ratings, against both individual experts and expert averages, to establish agreement and validity.

  • Develop hybrid scoring pipelines with engineering that combine human oversight with AI scoring.

  • Evaluate and calibrate psychometric models for validity and comparability across populations and test forms.

4. Bias and fairness analysis

  • Detect and analyse bias in AI-generated and psychometric scores across demographic groups, including subgroup analysis.

  • Apply mitigation techniques such as reweighting and calibration without losing model performance.

  • Contribute to fairness dashboards and compliance documentation that support transparent model governance.

5. Predictive analytics and performance insights

  • Model the relationship between candidate scores and job performance and retention, using large assessment and performance datasets.

  • Develop and test models that estimate success probabilities or identify behavioural and linguistic predictors of performance.

  • Work with data science, implementation and customer success teams to turn findings into recommendations for clients and colleagues.

6. Research output

  • Publish reports, papers and conference presentations, internal and external.

  • Explain technical findings clearly to non-technical colleagues and clients.

As one of Maki People's early employees, you'll help shape the team's future.

Our Ideal Candidate

Required

  • PhD or MSc in machine learning, computational linguistics, data science or psychology.

  • A track record of publications, such as peer-reviewed papers or conference papers.

  • Hands-on experience evaluating LLMs: designing benchmarks, measuring agreement with human raters, and testing consistency and robustness of model output.

  • Experience testing AI-driven decisions for fairness and bias.

  • Proficiency in Python or R, with experience in statistical analysis.

  • Clear communication of results to scientific and business audiences.

Preferred

  • Experience with NLP techniques for automated scoring.

  • Experience fine-tuning language models, for example with LoRA.

  • Experience working with cloud databases and large datasets.

  • Working knowledge of psychometric concepts such as reliability, validity and IRT, and how they apply to assessment design and validation.

  • Working knowledge of ethical AI, data governance and compliance, such as the EU AI Act.

  • Experience working with engineering, product and content teams.

Application Process

  • Stage 1 - Screening assessment (25 min)

  • Stage 2 - Power skill assessment with our AI agent (15 min)

  • Stage 3 - Hiring manager interview (45 min)

  • Stage 4 - Executive interview (45 min)

  • Stage 5 - Deep-dive technical interview (60 min)

title: AIT Systems Integration Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.

You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch.

The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.

Responsibilities

Functional and system testing

  • Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.

  • Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.

  • Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.

  • Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.

  • Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.

  • Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.

Verification tracking

  • Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.

  • Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.

  • Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.

  • Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.

GSE and test infrastructure

  • Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.

  • Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.

  • Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.

Integration and campaign support

  • Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.

  • Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.

  • Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.

  • Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.

Requirements

  • Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.

  • Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.

  • Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.

  • Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.

  • Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.

  • Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.

  • Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.

  • Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.

  • Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).

  • Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.

Desirables

  • End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.

  • Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).

  • Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).

  • Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.

  • Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).

  • Launch campaign experience at a launch site.

  • Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.

  • Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.

Personal attributes

  • Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.

  • Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.

  • Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.

  • Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.

  • Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.

Why NewOrbit Space?

  • Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

  • Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

  • Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

  • Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

title: Algorithm Engineer (m/f/d)
descriptionHtml:
What is Anori Tech doing?

The world talks about batteries, cells and the energy transition. Almost nobody talks about the Battery Management System (BMS) that makes them work.

As battery applications multiply, from robotics and mobility to data centers and grid-scale storage, BMS complexity is exploding. Legacy BMS architectures were never built for this: too rigid to keep up with new requirements, they've turned the BMS into the bottleneck of battery development.

We're building something different: a novel software-defined BMS architecture combined with an AI-driven configuration process. It gets battery manufacturers the right BMS for their exact use case within days, regardless of application or cell chemistry.

We're building the battery management system platform of tomorrow. Delivered in days, not years.

Join us and shape one of the fastest growing markets in the energy sector: The BMS market.

Our Motivation

At Anori Tech, we believe everything is energy, and progress runs on it. With Anori we actively shape the energy transition: from oil to electric, from low to high efficiency. We need batteries for this transition and almost all batteries need a BMS. We strive for Shenzhen speed and German engineering quality. Our objective: put Europe back on the map in the race for the energy transition and build technical leadership out of Hamburg.

About the Role

A BMS is only as good as what it knows about the battery. As our Algorithm Engineer, you'll develop the algorithms that tell the Anori BMS what is happening inside the cells: state of charge, state of health and balancing. And you won't stop at the concept: you'll design algorithms, implement them in our embedded Rust firmware and validate them on real hardware. Later on, the role grows into the cloud, where data pipelines and fleet analytics will build on the models you create today. You'll work closely with Stefan, our CTO, and our firmware and hardware engineers.

Start date: from January 1, 2027

What You'll Do

  • Develop the algorithms that estimate SoC and SoH for different cell chemistries and applications

  • Design balancing strategies that fit the hardware and use case

  • Build battery models (e.g. equivalent circuit models) and parameterize them from measurement data with statistical rigor

  • Implement your algorithms directly in the embedded Rust firmware, efficient enough for constrained hardware

  • Design experiments and evaluation methodologies: analyze failure modes, quantify trade-offs between accuracy, robustness and compute cost

  • Support in building data pipelines and fleet analytics in the cloud

What You Bring

Must have

  • Hands-on experience with state of charge and state of health estimation, shown in a product, publication or substantial project. For example Kalman-type filters, H∞ filters, observers, or coulomb counting with model-based correction

  • Deep understanding of battery behavior and modeling, e.g. equivalent circuit models, hysterisis, ageing or also physics based models

  • Experience implementing numerical algorithms on embedded, constrained hardware (e.g. in Rust or C/C++ - heads-up our firmware is written in Rust, and we'll help you get up to speed)

  • Strong Python skills for modeling, simulation and data analysis

  • Critical, analytical, systematic thinking: you reason from first principles, make your assumptions explicit and challenge existing paradigms

Strongly preferred

  • Experience with cell balancing algorithms and their effects

  • Working with real cell data from test benches or cyclers

  • Signal processing fundamentals: FIR/IIR filter design, sampling and aliasing, noise characterization of sensor data

Nice to have

  • Data pipelines, fleet analytics or cloud experience

  • Machine learning methods for battery data, for example data-driven state of health estimation or anomaly detection

  • Model-based systems engineering and requirements engineering (the skills, not the paper)

You don't tick every box? Apply anyway. No one matches a job description 100%. If this role excites you and you are motivated to grow yourself into it, we want to hear from you.

What We Offer

  • Work on a product with purpose that redefines the state of art: our product is a key part to enable competitive battery energy storage.

  • Work directly with the founding team on decisions that shape the company. The team is small, so your ideas will matter. A lot.

  • Challenging engineering in an industrial, but research-near environment. We bring research into the industry.

  • A modern stack and methods: Rust, MBSE, everything as code, and the best tools and techniques for the job, chosen on merit.

  • To be both supported and challenged: room to grow, and the expectation that you will.

You might be a fit if

  • You hold yourself to a high standard and don’t settle for "good enough."

  • You want to have a big say in what the Anori BMS looks like and how it works

  • You are eager to try out new tools and enjoy incorporating AI into your work to make your life easier and more productive

  • You are excited about startups and all the opportunities and uncertainties that come with it

  • You want to be an active part in accelerating the energy transition in Europe

  • You are comfortable with English as a working language

  • You are happy to be in the office most of the time because for fast decisions we need to be in the same room. We expect you to be in the office at least 3 days / week

You also want to become an Anori? We cannot wait to meet you. Go and click the apply button. Don’t be shy, we are nice.

P.S. Extra bonus if you tell us what your favorite type of tea is.

descriptionHtml:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for applied AI engineers to build AI-native systems for BJAK's AI Finance Agent.

This is not a research-only role. We need builders who can use AI to automate real workflows, improve products, reduce manual work and make financial services easier for users and teams.

What You'll Own

  • Build AI-powered workflows, assistants, agents and automation systems.

  • Apply AI across customer support, CRM, onboarding, claims, renewals, payments, operations and internal tools.

  • Work with product and engineering teams to turn manual processes into scalable AI-native systems.

  • Build integrations with LLMs, internal data, APIs, documents, knowledge bases and business systems.

  • Design evaluation, monitoring and fallback flows so AI outputs are useful, safe and reliable.

  • Prototype quickly, test with users or operators, then productionize what works.

  • Improve speed, quality and consistency across workflows using AI where it creates real business value.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering foundation, preferably with Python and backend systems.

  • Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs, agents, RAG, workflow automation or AI tools.

  • Able to connect AI systems with real product, data and operational workflows.

  • Good judgement on where AI helps and where rule-based systems or human review are better.

  • Understands evaluation, accuracy, latency, cost, privacy and failure modes.

  • Fast builder who can prototype, test and ship practical systems.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, support automation, CRM or operations automation is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Practical AI builder, not just a prompt experimenter.

  • Thinks in workflows, systems and measurable quality.

  • Can build quickly but still cares about guardrails and reliability.

  • Comfortable working with messy real-world data and processes.

  • Honest about what AI can and cannot do.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want research projects with no production ownership.

  • Candidates who treat AI as demos instead of working systems.

  • Engineers who do not care about evaluation, reliability or user impact.

  • People who overclaim AI impact without evidence.

  • Builders who cannot work with product, ops and business teams.

Location

This role is based in the UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our UK office at least 3 days per week.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

descriptionHtml:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied AI Engineer based in France.

As an Applied AI Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and building the next generation of intelligent, agentic systems.
You will develop the core infrastructure that enables AI agents to manage context, use tools, coordinate tasks, and continuously improve their performance.
Working at the intersection of advanced AI research and practical software engineering, you will transform complex operational workflows into reliable, scalable production solutions.
You will establish robust evaluation, testing, and observability frameworks to ensure AI-powered systems deliver predictable and measurable results.
You will also explore innovative ways to integrate coding agents and specialized subagents into software development processes.
Collaborating closely with product and operational teams, you will identify high-impact automation opportunities and translate them into effective technical solutions.
As an early core member of the engineering team, you will have significant influence over architectural decisions, technical standards, and the long-term AI strategy.


Accountabilities

In this role, you will design and implement the technical foundations of agentic systems while driving the adoption of AI-powered engineering workflows. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Design and build essential components of agentic systems, including memory, context management, tool-calling capabilities, orchestration mechanisms, and feedback loops.

  • Develop reusable AI infrastructure that enables new workflows to be introduced quickly, consistently, and with predictable reliability.

  • Build comprehensive evaluation frameworks to measure agent performance, identify failure points, and understand the factors behind successful outcomes.

  • Establish scalable architectural patterns and engineering standards for agentic systems as the organization grows.

  • Take ownership of technical decisions and contribute to the overall direction of the AI engineering function.

descriptionHtml:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. title: Associate Director, Biostatistics Consultant – Oncology - (Remote in UK- Outside IR35)
descriptionHtml:
Are you interested in working directly for a single sponsor while having the security and additional career opportunities that working for a global CRO can bring? Our team says it’s the best of both worlds….

ClinChoice is searching for a Associate Director, Biostatistics Consultant  – Oncology to join one of our clients. 

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Associate Director, Biostatistics with strong expertise in oncology drug development and clinical trial strategy. The individual will provide strategic statistical leadership across development programs and work closely with Clinical Development, Regulatory, Medical, Commercial, and Portfolio teams.

The ideal candidate should have experience in:

  • Selecting Trial Types: decide if a trial should be superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence-based depending on what regulators and payers need to prove the drug beats a placebo or standard of care.
  • Endpoint Selection: define and validate primary and secondary endpoints (e.g., overall survival, biomarker response rates, quality-of-life scores) to ensure they are measurable, clinically meaningful, and statistically robust.
  • Innovative Designs: statisticians frequently design adaptive trials (e.g., seamless Phase II/III designs, group sequential designs, or biomarker-driven basket/umbrella trials) to save time and patients.
  • Sample Size & Power Calculations
  • Balancing Risk and Resources:  use power calculations to ensure a trial has a high probability of detecting a true clinical effect without enrolling excess patients, which drives up costs and exposes unnecessary individuals to experimental risks.
  • Subgroup Powering: They determine if the study is large enough to analyze specific patient subsets (e.g., biomarker-positive patients or specific age groups).
  • Establishing Go/No-Go Decision Gates
  • Proof-of-Concept Criteria: establish quantitative thresholds for Phase II trials (e.g., "If the hazard ratio is below 0.70 with a p-value , we proceed to Phase III").
  • Futility Stopping Rules: Experience in build rules into trial protocols to stop a failing trial early, preventing sunk costs on a drug that is unlikely to succeed.
  • Regulatory Strategy and Health Authority Negotiations : experience in preparing and reviewing data packages and attending meetings with regulatory bodies (like the FDA or EMA) to defend trial designs, proposed endpoints, and statistical analysis plans (SAPs).
  • Mitigating Regulatory Risk: Experience in anticipating and addressing statistical objections from health authorities regarding missing data handling, multiplicity adjustments (controlling for false positives when looking at multiple endpoints), and bias.

At the macro–Strategic Drug Development level, statisticians should have experience working with commercial and portfolio management teams.

  • Quantifying Uncertainty: Experience in using historical benchmark data and simulation models to estimate the Probability of Technical Success (PoS) for an asset at each development phase.
  • Pipeline Prioritization: Using risk models to help executive leadership in deciding whether to advance, partner, or kill an asset based on its statistical likelihood of clearing regulatory and market hurdles.

Qualifications

  • Master's or Ph.D. in Statistics, Biostatistics, or a related quantitative discipline.

  • Significant experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO environments with strong oncology experience.

  • Demonstrated experience in strategic drug development and clinical trial design, beyond traditional study-level responsibilities.

  • Strong knowledge of oncology endpoints, adaptive designs, sample size/power, simulations, and statistical methodology.

  • Experience supporting regulatory submissions and health authority interactions.

  • Excellent communication and leadership skills with the ability to influence senior cross-functional stakeholders.

The Application Process

Once you have submitted your CV, you will receive an acknowledgement that we received it. If you have the requirements we need, you will be invited for phone interview as the first step.  Unfortunately, due to the number of applications we receive, we cannot reply to everyone individually if you are not successful.

Who will you be working for?

About ClinChoice

ClinChoice is a global full-service CRO specializing in clinical development and functional solutions for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and consumer health companies. We have over 28 years of proven high-quality delivery and results across all our services, with over 4,000 professionals in more than 20 countries across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.           

Our Company Ethos

Our mission drives our culture: to contribute to a healthier and safer world by accelerating the development and commercialization of innovative drugs and devices. title: Associate Director, Corporate Strategy & Development (all genders)
descriptionHtml:
The role

As an Associate Director, Corporate Strategy & Development, you will be a senior member of a small, AI enabled team of highly driven and committed individuals, reporting to the Director Corporate Strategy & Development. This is a high-exposure role, acting as the strategic and analytical engine for our most important decisions in a team that reports directly to the Group CEO.

This role balances corporate development / M&A with corporate strategy. You lead projects across both areas as the day-to-day owner and guide a small number of more junior colleagues and internal functional experts. You operate with minimal direction and take projects from a vague problem statement to a CEO-ready recommendation. You also stay hands-on, personally building the models and analysis and preparing the executive-level outputs that drive investment and strategy decisions.

What you’ll do

  • M&A Strategy: Lead M&A projects end to end (owning small and mid-sized transactions independently and partnering with the Director on the largest, transformational deals), from target screening and valuation through due diligence, negotiation preparation, and post-deal integration. Run deal teams day to day, coordinate external advisors and act as the lead with target management teams or their advisors. You are not just a process manager but can form and defend a point of view on whether and why a deal makes strategic sense and present it directly to senior leadership.
  • Portfolio Optimization: Lead the strategic analysis and recommendations for key portfolio decisions, including potential geo-expansions, new vertical or brand launches or divestments.
  • Corporate Strategy: Contribute to the development of the Group's mid-term strategy by driving the process, owning the underlying analysis, strategic synthesis, and preparation of strategic documents.
  • Capital Allocation: Own and develop analytical frameworks and models to support strategic budget allocation and ROI analysis.
  • Business Unit Strategy: Act as a senior internal consultant, supporting our key business units across geographies on a project-by-project basis to develop their mid-term strategies and solve their most complex challenges.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience: 6+ years of high-performance experience from a top-tier Management Consulting firm, Investment Banking, or a comparable in-house Strategy / Corporate Development team. This includes leading projects or deal teams with minimal supervision.
  • Process and deal leadership: You have led complex, multi-stakeholder processes to a deadline, coordinating internal functions and external advisors and managing senior counterparties such as target or client management teams. This can come from running M&A transactions (in-house corporate development or advisory) or from leading strategy projects with transaction exposure, such as due diligence, carve-outs, partnerships or market entries. Direct M&A process experience is a strong plus; the ability to learn it quickly is essential.
  • Leadership and Influence: You have guided and developed more junior colleagues and influenced senior stakeholders, including through negotiation and building rapport with counterparties.
  • Toolkit: Exceptional qualitative and analytical problem-solving skills. You are hypothesis-driven and can own and structure complex analytical problems from end-to-end. You structure ambiguous problems and set direction for others, not just solve them yourself. You are utilizing AI tools to meaningfully improve your productivity. Ability to build applications with AI coding tools is a plus.
  • Financial Acumen: Expert-level financial modeling skills are required: you have built and defended complex models used for high-stakes investment or strategic decisions. Valuation experience is a plus. You are just as comfortable building analysis and models from scratch as you are managing processes and presenting recommendations to leadership.
  • DTC economics: You are comfortable working with typical DTC KPIs like CAC, AOR, AOV, CLV, retention and understand how cohort economics build a P&L over time. DTC marketing analytics experience is a plus but not required.
  • Communication: Proactive 360° communication and excellent ability to synthesize complex analysis into clear, concise storylines, presentationsand memos for an executive audience. 
  • How you work: You take ownership of outcomes and pressure-test your own conclusions before presenting them. You go deep into the analysis to get to the right answer, and know when it is good enough to decide. 

What you will get in return:

  • 70% off HelloFresh or Green Chef boxes
  • Company pension scheme
  • Gym membership
  • Bupa private medical insurance (including dental & family cover options)
  • Mental health first aiders and an employee assistance programme
  • Nursery support scheme
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Group Life Assurance

Location: The HelloFresh Farm, 60 Worship Street, EC2A 2EZ, London

Hybrid Working Policy
We offer a hybrid working policy for eligible roles, allowing flexibility to work from home and in the office. For more details on eligibility and how this applies to the role you're applying for, please consult with your recruiter.

Next steps: Your application will be reviewed and if successful, a member of the Talent Acquisition Team will be in touch within 2 weeks.

To be considered for this role, you’ll need to have the independent right to work in the UK, as we're unfortunately unable to provide sponsorship at this time.

You are required to cooperate with HelloFresh in all health and safety matters. You are responsible for ensuring you take reasonable care of your own health, and safety as well as others who may be affected by the work activities you undertake. You must report incidents immediately and actively raise health and safety-related concerns to your Line Manager. As part of our commitment to maintaining a safe and secure environment, we will process Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks to the successful individual. Failure to disclose relevant information at application or throughout the process could affect your employment with the company.

title: Associate
descriptionHtml:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the team:

Bringing medicine to patients is complex, expensive and high-risk. Faculty’s Life Science’s team is concentrated on building AI solutions which optimise the research and commercialisation of life-changing therapies.

We partner with major pharma firms, academic research centres, biotechs and MedTech companies to design and deliver solutions which address critical healthcare challenges.

 

About the role:

This is an exciting, new role, for an individual motivated to deepen their knowledge of AI transformation in life sciences. As an Associate, you’ll be part of a close-knit team - scoping, building and delivering impactful AI projects for our pharmaceutical clients. We’ll look to you to build trusted client relationships, analyse requirements and feedback, stay on top of workflows and help to ensure our bespoke AI solutions are optimised for real-world operations.

#LI-PRIO

 

What you'll be doing:

  • Managing individual work streams to support the successful delivery and implementation of bespoke AI solutions.

  • Working side-by-side with life sciences stakeholders to understand critical mission challenges and user needs

  • Conducting open-source analysis to support the development of cutting-edge AI tools

  • Translating complex operational requirements into clear user stories for delivery and engineering teams.

  • Designing and testing workflows that support user-centric decision-making in high-stakes environments

  • Collaborating closely with technical teams to ensure projects run smoothly and solutions meet customer needs

  • Contributing to internal thought leadership, strategy, and capability development across the team

 

Who we're looking for:

  • You have some experience working on AI implementation/data intensive projects in a commercial setting

  • You've worked in a Life Sciences company, or with Life Sciences clients

  • You demonstrate analytical thinking, can clearly communicate ideas, and synthesise complex information

  • You have external client-facing experience and have built trusted relationships which have contributed to the overall success of projects

  • You understand Agile and related methodologies and the basis of iterative development and continuous delivery

Our interview process:

  1. Talent Team Screen (40 mins)

  2. Introduction Interview (60 mins)

  3. Case Study Interview (60 mins)

  4. Interview with Business Unit Director (30 mins)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

title: Automations Lead
descriptionHtml:
You use AI and automation to make Pivotal's work faster and better, so that the team can do more without growing as fast.

  • Salary: £86,750–£155,500 per year, depending on seniority. We may be able to pay more for exceptional candidates.

  • Location: London, at our office at LISA

  • Hours: Full time

  • Visa: We can sponsor a Skilled Worker visa, but approval isn't guaranteed.

Why work at Pivotal

Pivotal finds people who can work on the biggest risks from advanced AI and gets them working on them. Since 2024, 135 fellows have taken part in our fellowships, and alumni now work at METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI and GovAI. We have grown from 2 staff in 2024 to 10 today, and we plan to reach at least 16 in 2027. Read more about us at pivotal-research.org, and about what it is like to work here.

What you will own

You’ll make the rest of the team faster & better by building & running the AI tools and automations behind our applications, fellow management, operations, etc. The goal is that Pivotal can run more and better programs without its team growing at the same rate. The AI safety field must grow a lot, and this will help Pivotal scale to support this growth.

We expect you to spend about 30% of your time making our existing tools better and more reliable. The rest goes to new tools. You talk to team members about what costs them the most time, tools they wish existed, and ship solutions quickly. Every tool has to meet our quality bar, protect personal data, and follow data protection law and our internal rules for AI use.

You might also be a central figure in a planned program on ‘AI for AI Safety’.

  • Internal tools. Build and maintain automations and AI agents for applications, fellow management, operations and reporting.

  • Application screening tools. Maintain the AI graders, check them for bias and errors, and design the human review steps around them.

  • Data. Keep applicant, fellow and alumni data clean and connected, so that we can measure outcomes.

  • Safe handling of data. Make sure our tools protect personal data and follow data protection law. You’ll have access to legal advice for this.

  • AI use across the team. Help staff, and fellows, use AI tools well.

Who does well in this role

  • Strong software engineering skills, and experience building tools with large language models and AI agents.

  • You talk to users, find the work that matters most, and ship quickly.

  • You care about reliability, security and data protection.

  • You can explain technical trade-offs in plain language.

  • You care about reducing catastrophic risks from AI.

We don’t expect anyone to be strong in all of this. If the role excites you, please apply, even if you match only part of what we describe here.

How we hire

We review applications as they come in, so applying early helps. The process has these stages:

  • Written application. A short form and your CV. It takes about 30 minutes.

  • Automated video interview. About 10 minutes. You record short answers to a few questions, at a time that suits you.

  • Work task. About 2 hours, based on real work in this role. We pay you for this time. You may use AI tools, as you would in the job. Tell us which ones you used and how.

  • Personal interview. About 45 minutes. We discuss your work task and how you would approach the role. With your consent, we record it so that more of the team can review it.

  • Work trial and references. Up to three paid days working with us at our office in London. We also speak to two referees, after asking you.

If you need an adjustment at any stage, such as extra time, tell us and we will arrange it. If you have questions, email ----- £86,750 – £155,500

title: Bilanzbuchhalter / Referent Rechnungswesen (m/w/d) in Vollzeit
descriptionHtml:
Wir stellen uns vor!

Die Dr. Bernhard Burger AG ist ein wachsendes Familienunternehmen in zweiter Generation und einer der führenden Partner für Goldschmiede, Juweliere und Edelmetallhändler. Gemeinsam mit unserem Joint Venture Burger & Gyr Edelmetalle Recycling AG am selben Standort in Keltern, zwischen Pforzheim und Karlsruhe, verbinden wir Edelmetallrecycling, Analyse, Abrechnung, Metallkonten, Handel und eigene Fertigung.

Unser Rechnungswesen bildet die Werteflüsse beider Gesellschaften ab: von der Scheidgutabrechnung über Metallkonten bis zu Monats- und Jahresabschluss. In den nächsten zwei Jahren führen wir ein neues, voll integriertes ERP-System auf Odoo-Basis ein. Damit wachsen die Themen, die wir kaufmännisch sauber durchdenken, abstimmen und zu Ende bringen müssen.

Deshalb suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine Persönlichkeit mit betriebswirtschaftlichem Überblick, die der kaufmännischen Leitung in Abschlüssen, Steuern, Finanzierung und Projekten spürbar Arbeit abnimmt, in der Buchhaltung selbst mit anpackt und tatkräftig im ERP-Projekt mitarbeitet. Einen Jahresabschluss müssen Sie nicht allein erstellen, aber wesentliche Abschlussarbeiten sicher übernehmen und mit Steuerberatern und Wirtschaftsprüfern intensiv zusammenarbeiten.

Wir messen Erfolg daran, dass Abschlüsse und Meldungen für beide Gesellschaften termingerecht und nachvollziehbar vorliegen, dass die kaufmännische Leitung bei Koordination und Zuarbeit entlastet wird und dass unsere Prozesse nach der ERP-Einführung einfacher und sicherer laufen als heute.

Die Stelle in Kürze

Sie übernehmen wesentliche Abschlussarbeiten für zwei Gesellschaften, entlasten unsere kaufmännische Leitung bei Steuern, Finanzierung und Analysen und begleiten als Key User die Einführung unseres neuen ERP-Systems auf Odoo-Basis.

Welche Aufgabenfelder erwarten Sie?

Ihr Schwerpunkt ist die Bilanzbuchhaltung. Im ERP-Projekt sind Sie Key User Rechnungswesen/Finanzen: Sie begleiten den Fortschritt, testen, ob alles wie vorgesehen funktioniert, denken und handeln mit und übernehmen bei Bedarf eigene Aufgaben oder Teilprojekte. Die Projektverantwortung bleibt bei unserer kaufmännischen Leitung.

  • Mitwirkung an Monats-, Quartals- und Jahresabschlüssen nach HGB für zwei Gesellschaften: Abschlussbuchungen, Kontenabstimmungen, Rückstellungen, Anlagenbuchhaltung, Datenaustausch mit Steuerberatern und Wirtschaftsprüfern

  • Unterstützung der kaufmännischen Leitung in allen betriebswirtschaftlichen Themen: Analysen, Auswertungen, Unterlagen für Vorstand und Banken, Vertrags- und Finanzierungsfragen
  • ERP-Einführung: Anforderungen der Finanzen mitformulieren, Prozesse dokumentieren, Stammdaten abgleichen, Tests durchführen, Key User Finanzen
  • Besonderheiten der Edelmetallbranche kennenlernen und mitgestalten: Metallkonten, Reverse Charge, Metallbilanz, Bestandsbewertung
  • Prozesse im Rechnungswesen weiterentwickeln und automatisieren, dabei selbst anpacken: vom Beleg bis zur Abschlussbuchung, perspektivisch eigene Verantwortungsbereiche und fachliche Koordination im Team

Was zeichnet Sie aus?

title: Biobank Lead (Senior Manager / Associate Director)
descriptionHtml:
About the role

Quotient is seeking an experienced, detail-oriented operational leader to run the management, process control, governance and quality leadership of its research tissue bank. Quotient's human tissue bank is the foundation of our proprietary high-resolution somatic genetics platform, which delivers insights into cellular and organ disease biology and discovers novel targets for the development of new medicines.

You will lead across the whole sample lifecycle, from procurement review and receipt through storage, use, reuse, transfer and disposal, and keep Quotient compliant with its Human Tissue Authority (HTA) research licence.

Reporting to the Head of Research Strategy and Operations, you will work closely with the Director of Partnerships to check that proposed research fits the permissions and restrictions attached to each collection. You will also be the central point of coordination between laboratory teams, Facilities, Procurement and Logistics, Project Leads and Data Infrastructure, so that colleagues get timely access to suitable samples with full end-to-end traceability.

This role combines ownership of the tissue bank with practical oversight of delivery. Success means reliable, well-organised inventory and chain-of-custody records, timely availability of samples for research, compliance with internal SOPs and HTA regulations, and effective resolution of any sample-related incidents.

Key responsibilities

  • Biobank governance and strategy: Own Quotient's research tissue bank strategy, aligning governance, capacity, resources and operating systems with the research portfolio, and recommend investment and improvements. Report sample availability, integrity, traceability, compliance risks and incident trends to leadership.
  • HTA compliance: Act as the HTA Designated Individual for Quotient's research licence, supervising licensed activities and making sure that staff, premises, storage and procedures meet HTA requirements. Develop SOPs, oversee training and competency assurance, and lead inspection readiness and responses, covering UK HTA, GDPR, research ethics and health and safety standards.
  • Sample access and use authorisation: Review access, initial use, reuse and onward transfer against consent, research ethics approvals, licence scope and contractual permissions, and document each decision. Apply independent judgement to complex sample-use decisions, balancing scientific priorities with donor permissions, sample availability and governance requirements, and obtain specialist advice or further approvals where needed.
  • Sample acquisition and custody: Own custody controls from handover at receipt through registration, storage, retrieval, distribution and disposal, including manifests, shipment conditions, acceptance checks, handovers and receipt acknowledgements. Set requirements for human tissue shipments and approve the release of inbound and outbound shipments, working with logistics colleagues who handle couriers and documentation. Provide cover for sample receipt and shipping, directly or through trained delegates.
  • Inventory systems and traceability: Integrate sample inventory with LIMS and ELN records, keeping identifiers, parent–derivative relationships, quantities, locations, status and movement histories accurate through timely updates, controlled access and periodic reconciliation. Ensure accurate annotation and metadata for all biospecimens, work with the Data Infrastructure team to bring sample data into research pipelines, and report on utilisation, inventory status and operational metrics.
  • Storage integrity and continuity: Manage storage organisation and capacity with laboratory and facilities colleagues. Work with the team that owns the temperature-monitoring system to make sure it is fit for purpose and supports HTA compliance, sign off monitoring procedures and the training of staff who use it, and check calibration and alarm-test records as part of routine internal audits. Own specimen decisions during alarms and recovery, including integrity assessment, transfers, holds and incident recording, and agree documented default actions so that out-of-hours response does not wait for a specimen decision.
  • Incident resolution and corrective action: Escalate concerns, pause non-compliant activities and hold samples where eligibility, documentation or integrity is unresolved. Run a quality-driven incident process, track corrective and preventive actions and approve closure.
  • Capability and culture: Build capability through coaching, knowledge sharing and effective cover arrangements across the biobank and sample-management network. Create an environment where colleagues raise concerns, learn from incidents and share accountability.

About you

You are an experienced biobanking or human tissue governance leader who combines sound regulatory judgement with practical delivery. You can make and explain proportionate decisions, influence across functions and build quality-based systems that support a growing research portfolio.

Essential criteria

  • BSc in Biological Sciences, Biomedical Sciences or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • More than 5 years working with human biological samples in a research, biotechnology, biobank or clinical laboratory setting, including leadership of sample governance and operations across the sample lifecycle.
  • Demonstrated leadership, including setting direction, developing colleagues and capability, influencing senior stakeholders without direct authority, and resolving competing priorities.
  • Experience working across a variety of quality systems, and able to interpret guidelines and apply basic principles in a research setting.
  • Experience reviewing consent, ethics and provenance documentation, interpreting sample-use restrictions, and assessing proposed use, reuse and transfer in collaboration with scientific, partnerships and legal colleagues.
  • Experience reviewing sample-related provisions in MTAs, SLAs, MSAs or equivalent agreements and translating those obligations into operational controls.
  • Proven ownership of sample accessioning, chain of custody, storage, database inventory and distribution processes, with practical experience of LIMS, ELN or comparable systems and their data quality and access controls.
  • Strong working knowledge of the Human Tissue Act 2004, HTA research licensing and relevant standards, with experience supporting or leading licensed activities.
  • Experience developing controlled documentation, training staff, preparing for audits or inspections, and leading incident investigations, corrective and preventive actions and documented closure.
  • Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail and professional judgement, with a commitment to donor respect, confidentiality, scientific quality and continuous improvement.

Desirable criteria

  • Previous appointment as an HTA Designated Individual, or substantial experience as a Person Designated with responsibility for tissue governance, inspections and compliance improvement.
  • Familiarity with handling low-complexity clinical data and associated regulatory frameworks (GDPR).
  • Experience in genomics, molecular biology or high-throughput research, including support for histology, flow cytometry or molecular workflows.
  • Experience with cryogenic storage, freezer monitoring, sample integrity assessment and business continuity arrangements.
  • Knowledge or experience of REC applications.
  • Experience coordinating domestic and international sample transfers, external biobanks, offsite sample storage companies or CROs, and working with third-party logistics teams within a growing biotechnology organisation.
  • Experience developing colleagues or leading a biobank or sample reception team, and implementing inventory platforms or significant process improvements.
  • Evidence of building or improving tissue bank processes and systems, planning capacity and resources, and balancing scientific delivery with ethical and regulatory responsibilities.

About Quotient:

Quotient Therapeutics is a privately-held, early stage company developing breakthrough medicines informed by natural somatic genetic diversity present in patients. Through our work in somatic genomics, we are forging a new status quo for biopharma research and development across a broad pipeline of internal and partnered programs. 

The company was founded by Flagship Pioneering, an innovative enterprise that conceives, creates, resources, and grows first-in-category life sciences companies. Flagship Pioneering has created over 100 groundbreaking companies over the past twenty years, all of which are pioneering novel and proprietary biological, industrial, and engineering approaches to solve major needs in human health and sustainability. These companies include Moderna (MRNA), Generate Biomedicines, Sana Biotechnology (SANA), Tessera Therapeutics, Evelo Biosciences (EVLO), Indigo Agriculture, Seres Therapeutics (MCRB), and Syros Pharmaceuticals (SYRS).

Quotient Therapeutics and Flagship Pioneering are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

Recruitment & Staffing Agencies:

Quotient Therapeutics (“Quotient”) and Flagship Pioneering (“FSP”) do not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to Quotient, FSP or their employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Flagship Pioneering’s internal Talent Acquisition team. Any resume submitted by an agency in the absence of a signed agreement will automatically become the property of FSP, and FSP will not owe any referral or other fees with respect thereto.

  • Personeelskorting op de volledige KEUNE-collectie.

KEUNE

We zijn een familiebedrijf met een langetermijnvisie, waar wetenschap centraal staat in alles wat we doen. Ons verhaal begint in 1922, in Amsterdam. Vandaag, 104 jaar later en een koninklijk predicaat rijker, hoort KEUNE bij één van de hardst groeiende merken in professionele haarverzorgingsproducten. Vanuit ons hoofdkantoor in Soest worden KEUNE-producten ontwikkeld, geproduceerd en wereldwijd gedistribueerd naar meer dan 85 landen. En we zijn niet van plan om gas terug te nemen! Ieder jaar openen we een nieuwe eigen vestiging. We produceren op een duurzame en diervriendelijke manier en zijn B Corp-gecertificeerd. Maar bij KEUNE gaat het niet alleen om het creëren van mooie producten - het gaat om ons verhaal en onze visie. KEUNE staat onder leiding van Philip Berlijn, die zich richt op het bouwen van een sterk merk en het creëren van een bedrijfscultuur die draait om samenwerken, duurzaamheid en het tonen van karakter.

title: Build Your Own Role – m/f/d
descriptionHtml:
Help Us Change the Way the World Works

 

Build something that matters.

Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe’s largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows, helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

 

About the Role

This is not a regular open application. We don’t want your CV first. We want to see what you have built.

You may build with AI because you can’t stop, whether that’s with Langdock, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or whatever gets the job done. You may also know you’d add real value at Langdock without seeing the right opening on our careers page. If both are true, this is your door.

Show us a project. If it convinces us, we build the role around you.

 

What We Want to See

Record a Loom of something you built with AI. It should be no longer than 5 minutes. Two kinds of projects get our attention:

  • Something that would help Langdock. Look at our product roadmap and at our product, and build something that solves a real problem for us or our customers. That could be a feature prototype, an internal tool, a GTM engine, a support automation, an eval setup, or something we haven’t thought of yet.

  • A genuine passion project. Something you built because you couldn’t stop thinking about it, and that shows how you think.

What we don’t want: basic chatbots, simple prompt wrappers, “summarize my inbox” agents, or linear three-step workflows. Our customers build those every day. Show us something that made you think hard, and that makes us think too.

 

What Your Loom Should Cover

  • The problem: what you solved and why it matters.

  • The demo: show it working live, not on slides.

  • How it’s built: the models, tools, architecture, and key decisions behind it.

  • What broke: where it failed and what you learned from that.

  • What’s next: what you would build at Langdock if you joined.

 

How to Apply

Paste your Loom link into the field “Your Build” in the application form. Your LinkedIn profile is enough; a CV is optional.

 

What Happens Next

We watch every Loom. If your build stands out, we invite you to go deep on your project with us. Together we then define where you would have the most impact. That could be Product, Engineering, GTM, Customer Success, Operations, or a role that doesn’t exist yet.

 

You Might Be a Fit If…

  • You build, not just talk about AI. You have shipped things that work, even if they’re rough.

  • You think in impact. You care about whether something solves a real problem for real users, not just whether it is technically clever.

  • You show high agency and full ownership. Nobody needs to tell you what to do next.

  • You experiment constantly. You try new models, tools, and approaches as soon as they come out.

  • You communicate clearly and professionally in English. German is a plus.

  • You are kind and care about the people around you.

 

What We Need

  • Availability to work full-time and 100% on-site at our Berlin office.

  • A work permit for Germany.

 

The Environment

You will work from our Berlin office at Greifswalder Straße 212, where all of us work together in person, surrounded by people building AI products and infrastructure every day. Lunch and dinner are catered in the office. We look after ourselves, and gym membership and coaching resources are part of the standard package. We value Calm Urgency, Ambitious Execution, and Caring Ownership. The vibe is calm but intense.

 

Compensation

Salaries are transparent and tied to levels, not negotiation. We define the level together once the role is clear.

 

Next Steps

We move fast. If you have built something you’re proud of, show us.

 

Compensation: €75K – €140K • Offers Equity

Was du mitbringst

  • Bereitschaft zu gelegentlichen Teamtreffen in Essen.

Das erwartet dich bei New Monday

  • Flexibles Arbeiten passend zum Projekt: In diesem Projekt arbeitest du überwiegend remote innerhalb Deutschlands. Gelegentliche Teamtreffen finden vor Ort in Essen statt.

  • Flexibilität und Vertrauen: Du organisierst deine Arbeit eigenständig und stimmst dich dabei mit deinem Kundenteam ab. Bei New Monday setzen wir auf kurze Abstimmungswege und Vertrauen.

  • Aufgaben mit Wirkung und Gestaltungsspielraum: Du bringst deine Erfahrung direkt im Kundenprojekt ein und gestaltest digitale Prozesse mit, die den Netzausbau und die Integration von Erzeugungsanlagen unterstützen.

  • Persönliche Begleitung im Projekteinsatz: Auch wenn dein Arbeitsalltag überwiegend im Kundenteam stattfindet, bleiben wir mit dir im Austausch und begleiten dich bei Fragen, Herausforderungen und deiner Entwicklung.

  • Ein Team, das sich auch persönlich trifft: Neben dem digitalen Austausch schaffen wir bewusst Raum für regionale Treffen und gemeinsames Coworking. Ein- bis zweimal im Jahr kommt das gesamte New-Monday-Team zusammen.

  • Zeit und Budget für deine Entwicklung: Wir fördern fachliche Weiterbildung und den Austausch im Team. Nach der Probezeit steht dir dafür ein Weiterbildungsbudget von 1.000 € zur Verfügung.

  • 30 Tage Urlaub und zusätzlich zwei Tage für unsere Team-Events.

So geht es weiter

  • Erstes Kennenlernen: Wir erzählen dir mehr über New Monday, die Rolle und das Kundenprojekt. Du berichtest uns von deiner Erfahrung und kannst alle Fragen stellen, die dir wichtig sind.

title: Business Development Intern
descriptionHtml:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

title: Business Development Manager
descriptionHtml:
Grosse Veränderungen beginnen mit Menschen, die mehr erreichen wollen.

Wie kommen Mitarbeitende zur Arbeit? Warum stehen Firmenautos ungenutzt herum, während Parkplätze knapp sind? Und wie wird nachhaltige Mobilität zur attraktivsten Wahl?

Bei Urban Connect machen wir aus diesen Herausforderungen konkrete Lösungen. Wir verbinden geteilte E-Bikes und Firmenautos, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel, Mobilitätsbudgets und digitales Parkplatzmanagement auf einer Plattform. Damit helfen wir Unternehmen, Kosten zu senken, Ressourcen besser zu nutzen und ihren Mitarbeitenden mehr Freiheit zu geben.

Unternehmen wie Roche, Google, SWISS und Lonza setzen bereits auf uns. Unser Anspruch geht weiter: Wir wollen die Art verändern, wie Unternehmen Mobilität organisieren. Und wir bieten das Betriebssystem, das dies möglich macht.

Um diese Vision zu verwirklichen, suchen wir eine neugierige, unternehmerisch denkende Persönlichkeit, die Verantwortung übernimmt, Energie und gutes Urteilsvermögen mitbringt und mit uns das Unternehmen und die Mobilitätsbranche voranbringen möchte.

Deine Rolle: echte Verantwortung, spürbare Wirkung

Du möchtest ein Unternehmen mitgestalten, anspruchsvolle Probleme lösen und sehen, was deine Arbeit bewirkt.

Als Business Development Manager arbeitest du eng mit unserem Sales- und Account-Management-Team sowie mit Product, Technology und Operations zusammen. Du entwickelst aus Kundenbedürfnissen, Daten und Marktkenntnissen überzeugende Mobilitätslösungen und konkrete Wachstumschancen.

Du verantwortest Projekte, bringst eigene Ideen ein und treibst ihre Umsetzung voran. Wir erwarten, dass du von Anfang an durchdachte Fragen stellst, erkennst, wo du einen Beitrag leisten kannst, und ins Handeln kommst. Dabei unterstützen dich Kolleginnen und Kollegen, die wollen, dass du erfolgreich bist.

Was du bei uns bewegst

  • Aus Daten Chancen machen: Du analysierst Nutzungs- und Marktdaten, etwa zur Auslastung von Fahrzeugen und Parkplätzen, und entwickelst daraus umsetzbare Empfehlungen für bessere betriebliche Mobilitätslösungen.

  • Eigene Projekte vorantreiben: Du verantwortest Projekte wie Produktanalysen, die Bewertung von Geschäftschancen und die Entwicklung betrieblicher Mobilitätskonzepte. Du definierst nächste Schritte, bringst die richtigen Menschen zusammen und erzielst Ergebnisse.

  • Das Produkt verstehen: Du entwickelst ein praxisnahes Verständnis unserer Plattform, der Kundeneinrichtung, Buchungen, Abrechnungen und Integrationen. So gestaltest du Lösungen mit, die wirtschaftlich und operativ funktionieren.

  • Mit KI besser arbeiten: Du setzt KI-Tools gezielt ein, testest neue Anwendungen und verbesserst die Qualität und Effizienz unserer Recherchen, Analysen und Prozesse.

  • Wachstum vorantreiben: Du identifizierst potenzielle Kunden, verstehst ihre Herausforderungen und arbeitest mit dem Commercial-Team daran, neue Kunden zu gewinnen und bestehende Partnerschaften auszubauen.

  • Überzeugend argumentieren: Du erstellst klare Präsentationen, fundierte Business Cases, überzeugende Angebote und aussagekräftige Kundenreviews, die den Mehrwert unserer Lösungen sichtbar machen.

  • Für Fortschritt sorgen: Du setzt klare Prioritäten und hältst Kundeninformationen und nächste Schritte in HubSpot aktuell. Du hältst Zusagen ein und gehst Hindernisse frühzeitig an.

  • Teams verbinden: Du klärst technische und kommerzielle Fragen gemeinsam mit Product, Operations und Technology und leitest daraus verständliche Empfehlungen für Kunden und das Team ab.

  • Den Status quo hinterfragen: Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenzial, hinterfragst Annahmen und machst aus kreativen Ideen konkrete Verbesserungen.

Was du mitbringst

  • Einen sehr guten akademischen Leistungsausweis, beispielsweise in Betriebswirtschaft, Volkswirtschaft, Data Science oder Ingenieurwissenschaften. Wissbegierde, Kreativität und nachweisbare Leistungen sind uns wichtiger als eine bestimmte Studienrichtung.

  • Relevante praktische Erfahrung im Business Development, in der Beratung, in einem Technologieunternehmen oder im unternehmerischen Umfeld. Du kannst zeigen, welche Projekte du verantwortet und welche Ergebnisse du erzielt hast.

  • Analytisches Denkvermögen, einen sicheren Umgang mit Excel und die Fähigkeit, komplexe Ideen und Zusammenhänge zu verstehen und klar und einfach zu erklären.

  • Grosses Interesse an der Mobilität der nächsten Generation und an den Technologien, Geschäftsmodellen und Verhaltensänderungen, die die Branche prägen. Idealerweise kennst du die betriebliche Mobilitätslandschaft bereits und hast Ideen, wie sie sich verbessern lässt.

  • Gutes Urteilsvermögen: Du kannst Zielkonflikte abwägen, Wesentliches priorisieren und vorankommen, ohne auf vollständige Informationen zu warten.

  • Tatkraft und einen kreativen Zugang zur Problemlösung. Du entwickelst Vorschläge, überprüfst Annahmen und findest Wege, Dinge voranzubringen.

  • Technologieaffinität und praktische Erfahrung mit KI-Tools wie ChatGPT, Claude oder Copilot sowie das Urteilsvermögen, deren Ergebnisse kritisch zu prüfen.

  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse. Französisch ist ein grosser Vorteil.

Besonders wichtig ist uns deine Haltung.

Du bringst Begeisterung, Ehrgeiz und eine lösungsorientierte Einstellung mit. Du lernst schnell, stellst durchdachte Fragen und übernimmst Verantwortung für Ergebnisse. Du achtest auf Details und suchst laufend nach Wegen, gute Arbeit noch besser zu machen.

Du bist selbstbewusst genug, eine Idee zu hinterfragen, und offen genug, deine Meinung zu ändern. Die beste Lösung und der Erfolg des Teams sind dir wichtiger als persönliche Anerkennung. Du suchst Feedback, teilst dein Wissen und arbeitest gerne mit Menschen zusammen, die das genauso halten.

Du probierst Neues aus, gehst bewusst Risiken ein und lernst aus Fehlern. Wenn du auf ein Problem stösst, ergreifst du die Initiative und beziehst andere ein, wenn es sinnvoll ist.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

Hohe Ansprüche – und kluge, herzliche Menschen, die dich fordern und weiterbringen.
Wir arbeiten ambitioniert, geben direktes, konstruktives Feedback und unterstützen uns gegenseitig. Exzellenz zeigt sich bei uns im Alltag: in durchdachten Lösungen, sorgfältiger Umsetzung und dem Willen, kontinuierlich besser zu werden.

Eine Rolle, die das ganze Unternehmen verbindet.
Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von Vertrieb, Customer Success, Technologie und Operations und hilfst dabei, aus Ideen Lösungen zu machen, die Kunden schätzen.

Verantwortung und Raum für Initiative.
Gute Ideen finden bei uns schnell Gehör. Du übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, Dinge voranzubringen, kannst auf die Unterstützung des Teams zählen und gestaltest mit, wie wir arbeiten.

Die Möglichkeit, mit Urban Connect zu wachsen.
Mit deinen Ergebnissen und Fähigkeiten wächst auch dein Verantwortungsbereich. Du hast die Chance, die nächste Entwicklungsphase unseres Unternehmens mitzugestalten.

Dazu kommen:

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten und ein schönes Büro in Zürich.

  • Ein monatliches Mobilitätsbudget sowie Zugang zu unseren E-Bikes und geteilten E-Autos.

title: CDI - Manager Product Engineer - Paris
descriptionHtml:
Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.

Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.
