title: Chief Customer Officer
descriptionHtml:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship.

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge.

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

title: Chief Engineer, Maritime
descriptionHtml:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

UFORCE is looking for a Chief Engineer to take end-to-end technical ownership of a priority product family, platform, or cross-product mission system spanning air, land, maritime, payloads, and enabling technologies.

Our systems have been shaped by extensive real-world operational use. The next challenge is to turn that advantage into globally deployable products that continuously improve, move rapidly from operator need to fielded capability, and can be produced reliably at scale.

You will be the accountable technical leader for the complete system: translating mission needs into requirements, leading architecture and design decisions across disciplines, driving performance improvements, and ensuring that products are integrated, testable, manufacturable, reliable, and ready for operational use. You will work closely with UFORCE's technical founder, Hardware and Software leadership, Product, Manufacturing, Delivery, and engineering teams across Ukraine and Global markets.

This is not a role for someone who wants to manage engineering from a distance. You will remain close to the technology, the people building it, and the operators using it - leading design reviews, supporting tests and deployments, resolving difficult system-level problems, and creating the technical clarity that allows strong engineers to move quickly.

The role is ideally based in the United Kingdom and will require regular travel to UFORCE engineering, manufacturing, test, and deployment locations.

What you'll do

  • Take end-to-end technical ownership of an assigned UFORCE product family, platform, or integrated mission system.

  • Translate operator needs, customer requirements, field evidence, and strategic priorities into clear system requirements, architecture, interfaces, and acceptance criteria.

  • Lead technical trade-offs across mechanical, electrical, electronics, controls, embedded software, autonomy, communications, payloads, power, manufacturing, and operational constraints.

  • Identify and deliver material improvements to mission performance, including areas such as range, endurance, payload, accuracy, survivability, speed, reliability, and operator effectiveness.

  • Accelerate the path from mission need to tested and fielded capability through rapid, evidence-led build-test-learn cycles.

  • Establish and maintain a coherent technical baseline across requirements, system architecture, interfaces, configurations, and regional product variants.

  • Ensure designs are manufacturable, testable, maintainable, supportable, and capable of being produced repeatedly at the required rate and quality.

  • Use test, deployment, exercise, operator, and combat evidence to diagnose failures, establish root causes, and drive verified corrective action.

  • Lead high-quality requirements, architecture, design, integration, test-readiness, and release-readiness reviews without introducing unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Build and develop a lean, high-performing cross-disciplinary engineering team with clear ownership, strong technical standards, and a low-ego approach to problem-solving.

  • Partner closely with Software Engineering and Pavel's organization to ensure hardware, software, controls, compute, and autonomy operate as one integrated system.

  • Personally intervene when a priority technical issue or programme is blocked and remain accountable until the system-level problem is resolved.

What we're looking for

  • Significant experience as a Chief Engineer, Chief Systems Engineer, Technical Director, Head of Engineering, Chief Designer, Engineering Director, or equivalent senior technical authority for a complex physical system.

  • Evidence of having owned a product or system through requirements, architecture, design, integration, verification, production release, and real-world operation.

  • Broad systems judgment across multiple engineering disciplines, with the ability to understand interactions, challenge assumptions, and lead consequential technical trade-offs.

  • A track record of materially improving system or product performance using first-principles engineering, structured experimentation, and objective evidence.

  • Experience shortening development or upgrade cycles in a high-consequence environment while maintaining appropriate safety, design assurance, configuration control, and verification.

  • Experience taking a complex product from prototype or low-volume development into repeatable production, or materially improving reliability, quality, yield, maintainability, cost, or throughput.

  • The technical credibility to lead highly capable specialists without needing to be the deepest expert in every discipline.

  • A leadership style that develops engineers, creates clear ownership, encourages constructive challenge, and treats failed hypotheses as a source of learning rather than blame.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving, globally distributed environment with incomplete structure, constrained resources, and rapidly changing priorities.

  • Willingness to work directly with engineers, factories, test teams, deployed personnel, customers, and operators wherever the most important technical problem exists.

Nice to have

  • Experience developing unmanned, autonomous, robotic, aerospace, maritime, defense, or other safety- or mission-critical systems.

  • Direct experience supporting military customers, live exercises, demonstrations, deployments, or operationally fielded products.

  • Experience in an engineering environment characterized by rapid iteration, tight performance margins, and demanding delivery cycles.

  • Familiarity with integrated hardware-software systems, embedded controls, autonomy, communications, payload integration, or system-of-systems architecture.

  • Experience adapting a common product architecture across countries, regulatory environments, supply chains, or customer-specific configurations.

  • Experience building or turning around an engineering team, function, or technical operating model in a startup or high-growth environment.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

Are You?

title: Chief Financial Officer
descriptionHtml:
Fastned is on a mission to accelerate the transition to electric mobility. Since 2012, we have been building and operating a rapidly growing network of iconic fast-charging stations across Europe powered entirely by solar and wind energy. With 500+ colleagues, we now operate over 450+ stations across nine countries, with an ambitious goal of reaching 1,000 stations by 2030. We are not building infrastructure for its own sake. Every station we open is a tangible step in the transition away from fossil fuels.

We are a listed company on Euronext Amsterdam, with a community of over 10,000 retail investors and a growing base of institutional funding partners. In 2025, we reported €122.4 million in charging revenue: a 47% year-on-year increase, exceeding €100 million in annual revenue for the first time. Fastned is at a pivotal point: growing fast, approaching profitability, and expanding across Europe. As our CFO, you will lead a talented and growing team of 40+ finance professionals to drive and shape Fastned's continued success.

Your Role

We are looking for a CFO to join the Management Board, alongside our CEO, COO and CCO, who will drive Fastned on its path to profitability while enabling further growth.

This role is for a financial leader who thrives in scale-up environments and feels comfortable navigating the complexity of an international matrix organisation. You know how to build a finance function that is both structured and able to move fast, effectively resolving scaling-bottlenecks along the way. You maintain strong financial discipline while enabling the continued investment needed to expand the charging network that supports our long-term vision.

In this role, you oversee the full Finance domain, developing people and teams to the next phase. You act as a key financial voice within the Executive Team and Management Board.

Your responsibilities will include:

Strategic Planning & Partnering: Partner with the Executive Board to set long-term financial goals, evaluate investment opportunities, oversee mergers and acquisitions and direct your teams to deliver the analyses and frameworks that underpin these decisions.

Manage our capital structure by optimising the company's capital, debt, and equity structure to maximise shareholder value.

Leading the Finance Domain: lead and inspire a talented Finance team of 43 professionals, bringing clear direction, fostering growth in culture that balances a bold mission with financial rigour. With your operational finance expertise, you will empower domain leads to do their best work. For each of your domains this entails the following:

  • Accounting & Reporting team: enabling finance transformation to ensure accurate and timely preparation of financial statements, ensuring full compliance with applicable regulatory standards and accounting frameworks.

  • Funding & Investor Relations team: develop a compelling, forward-looking equity story that reflects both current performance and long-term potential. You will serve as the primary spokesperson for Fastned's financial health, leading earnings calls and maintaining strong relationships with analysts, shareholders, and investors.

  • Business & Financial Control team: partner with Country- and Functional Directors to evaluate the business cases for new markets, charging stations, joint ventures, and other expansion initiatives, balancing rigorous financial discipline and cost efficiency with growth decisions.

  • Risk & Audit team: build structures that protect against financial fraud and operational risk. Represent the Management Board in Audit Committee meetings and actively drive the implementation and maintenance of internal controls.

  • Tax team: meet tax compliance and the maintenance of a tax control framework across all countries, covering corporate income tax, transfer pricing, and VAT.

  • Serve as the executive owner of Fastned's sustainability strategy, ensuring it is credible, auditable, and aligned with both regulatory requirements, the company's long-term mission.

Management Board Member: Serve as a full member of the Management Board, carrying statutory responsibility for Fastned's financial governance, risk management, sustainability reporting, and knowing when to accelerate growth and when to apply disciplined challenges.

Who we are looking for

  • A financial leader (RA, CPA, CIMA, ACA or equivalent) with proven experience in senior operational finance leadership in scale-up or high-growth environments.

  • A genuine people leader who inspires, challenges, and grows the people around them.

  • Experience in building and professionalising a scalable finance function, including systems, processes, and team capability including leveraging AI and digital technologies company-wide.

  • Bring a healthy appetite for risk combined with rigorous financial discipline: knowing when to accelerate and when to challenge, driving the business towards profitability while enabling sustainable growth.

  • Good understanding of fundingand capital markets including bonds, equity, project finance, or institutional investment with the ability to tell a compelling and credible financial story to investors.

  • Ability to articulate a long-term financial vision and translate it into clear near-term actions.

  • Affinity with Fastned's mission: a genuine belief in the energy transition.

Join us in building a better future

We work hard to change the world, but we don't forget to recognise & celebrate our successes, big and small. We put a focus on work-life balance, provide you with genuine work flexibility and have family-friendly policies in place.

Next to a wide range of attractive secondary benefits, your CFO comps & ben package includes:

  • Annual base compensation between EUR 180.000 and EUR 280.000 (including 8% holiday allowance).

  • You will participate in Fastned’s attractive stock option programmes designed to give you a meaningful opportunity to participate in the long-term value you help create as a member of Fastned’s Management Board.

  • Company-wide Performance Bonus: You are eligible for a discretionary annual bonus with a target of 15% of your annual base salary.

  • 29 holidays. Additionally, you will have 2 ‘Mission Days’ that you can use to contribute to Fastned’s mission or to support a cause that is important to you.

  • Fully electric company car.

Interested in making an impact?

We would love to have a conversation with you and hear why you’re excited about joining Fastned’s mission in this impactful role. Our talent acquisition team will get back to all applicants in due time to share details about timing & structure of the upcoming recruitment process.

Fastned stands for equity and inclusion. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, gender identities, sexual orientations, religions, neurodiversity, disabilities, parental status or any other protected characteristic that makes you unique.

A note to recruitment agencies: we work exclusively with a carefully selected party for this search. Unsolicited agency approaches or candidate submissions will not be considered and do not create any obligation on Fastned's part.

title: Chief of Staff, CFO
descriptionHtml:
About Airwallex

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 

About the team:

Finance & Corporate Development helps Airwallex grow with control. We’re a trusted partner to the business, providing actionable insights on performance, supporting market and product expansion and helping to shape the future of our product. We ensure that Airwallex meets its financial reporting, tax and safeguarding obligations globally. We work with existing and prospective investors to raise capital and ensure it is deployed effectively.

This is a team for people who want to reimagine how the office of the CFO works. We’re looking for founder-like energy, high integrity and a passion for technology. You’ll thrive here if you enjoy working cross-functionally, think from first principles and can balance speed of execution with analytical precision.

What you’ll do:

As Chief of Staff to our Group CFO, you’ll be the CFO’s right hand across three divisions: Finance & Corporate Development, People & Talent, and global Operations. You will run the operating rhythm that keeps those teams aligned, own the CFO’s most important projects from first framing to delivery, and help build a CFO-led programme that brings Airwallex closer to the finance leaders we serve.

You’ll work directly with the CFO, the CEO, the executive team and our investors.

This role is based in our London office.

Responsibilities:

  • Run the CFO’s operating cadences: Ensure the smooth running of the Finance, People & Talent and Operations divisions, driving divisional OKRs, business reviews, leadership team meetings and offsites.

Who you are:

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior experience as Chief of Staff to a C-Suite executive

  • Experience in payments, cross-border or another regulated financial services business.

  • Experience with M&A/corporate finance (including fundraising)

  • Experience building executive events or communities.

  • An entrepreneurial streak: you’ve founded a business or side project.

You’ll thrive here if:

  • You keep asking why until you feel like you really understand something

All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
descriptionHtml:
Mozilla Foundationis a non-profit building a better technology future — powered by people, open by design, fueled by imagination.

We deliver people-first alternatives to today’s extractive systems. We build side by side with developers, innovators and advocates, united in the belief that a better technology future is not only possible — it’s ours to create!

Team

Our CEO is increasingly focused outward on the Board, funders, partners, and public conversations that will shape the Foundation’s next chapter. This newly created Chief of Staff role exists to extend the CEO’s reach inside the organization and make that outward focus possible.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll serve as the CEO’s strategic partner, internal proxy and trusted extension of their leadership. You’ll hold the CEO’s strategic agenda, translate the CEO’s priorities into organizational alignment, represent the CEO internally where needed, and make decisions on the CEO’s behalf within clearly delegated authority. You’ll determine what reaches the CEO, prepare the CEO for consequential moments, and escalate only what requires the CEO’s judgment.

As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you’ll partner strategically with other members of the ELT and work closely with the CEO’s Executive Program Manager to make sure the CEO’s time, priorities, and commitments stay aligned and moving.

You’ll also partner with the Foundation’s Investment Committee and its technical and strategic advisors, keeping their focus on the right questions, their recommendations aligned with the Foundation’s strategic priorities, and decisions moving efficiently from evaluation to funding.

Job responsibilities

Here’s what you’ll likely be focused on for the first 6 months:

  • Building a strong working partnership with the CEO, aligning on priorities, ways of working and clearly defining the scope of your delegated authority.
  • Establishing a trusted partnership with each member of the Executive Leadership Team, learning their priorities, pressures and ways of working.
  • Developing a deep, cross-functional understanding of the Foundation’s work and how each function connects to the CEO’s priorities.
  • Translating the CEO’s priorities into a concise, clear set of strategic outcomes that leaders understand and can use to guide the decisions they own, with a current view of what’s changing and which decisions are approaching.
  • Defining with the CEO what truly requires their attention, and ensuring issues reach them decision-ready, with context, options and a recommendation.
  • Getting up to speed with the Investment Committee and its advisors, and helping keep their focus on the right questions so decisions move efficiently from evaluation to funding.

As the Chief of Staff to Mozilla Foundation’s CEO, you will…

  • Serve as the CEO’s thought partner in developing, pressure-testing and refining strategic priorities, synthesizing executive insight and external developments to anticipate what will need to be known or decided in the next 30, 60 and 90 days.
  • Direct the CEO’s time toward strategy, external relationships, development, Board leadership and the Foundation’s highest-consequence decisions.
  • Filter rather than forward, so significant shifts in strategy, material risks, major budget decisions and Board-level matters reach the CEO early, with context, options and a recommendation.
  • Maintain a current view of the CEO’s top priorities, identify where work is drifting from strategic intent, and surface conflicts in priorities, resources or attention before they become emergencies.
  • Enable the Executive Leadership Team to operate as one team around the CEO’s priorities, so the right issues reach the ELT at the right level and decisions and commitments are followed through.
  • Partner with ELT members on cross-functional issues that need CEO-level alignment but not the CEO’s direct involvement.
  • Represent the CEO’s position in internal discussions and make decisions on the CEO’s behalf within delegated authority, bringing anything beyond it back to the CEO promptly.
  • Ensure the CEO enters every Board meeting, funder and partner conversation, speech and public engagement fully prepared, with concise briefings, organizational context and answers to likely questions.
  • Identify external opportunities that warrant the CEO’s attention, and ensure commitments the CEO makes externally translate into clear internal follow-through.
  • Steward alignment between the Investment Committee’s work and the Foundation’s strategy: keep its technical and strategic advisors focused on the right questions, surface gaps, risks or competing views, and bring forward matters that need the CEO’s judgment.

What this role is not

This is a role of influence. It exists to ensure the CEO can lead effectively through the Executive Leadership Team.

  • The Chief of Staff does not manage the Executive Leadership Team or run the Foundation’s operations. Each executive leader owns execution and decisions within their area.
  • This role does not make decisions beyond the authority the CEO has delegated. Anything outside that authority returns to the CEO.
  • This role does not have any direct reports and also doesn’t manage the CEO’s calendar, scheduling or administrative support.

Your Professional Profile

  • Significant, verifiable experience as a strategic partner at CEO or executive-team level, with a track record of leading high-stakes work and turning ambiguity into structure and action.
  • Experience working across multiple legal entities is a plus, including navigating differences, building influence, and coordinating work across entities where relevant. 
  • A proven record of driving complex, cross-functional priorities from idea to execution by defining outcomes, ownership, milestones and decision points.
  • Exceptional judgment and discretion, including handling confidential information and navigating complex executive dynamics with integrity.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority, build trust across functions and at the most senior levels, and give direct feedback with care.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication, with experience distilling complex information into decision-ready briefs, recommendations, presentations and executive communications.
  • Strong analytical and strategic problem-solving skills: you frame the right question, gather the right information, test assumptions and recommend a practical path forward.
  • Disciplined prioritization, with the agility to move between long-term priorities and time-sensitive issues without losing the thread.
  • Direct experience supporting Board governance, fundraising or other high-stakes external relationships at an executive level.
  • A track record of doing high-impact work out of the spotlight, measuring your success by the CEO’s and the team’s, and acting in the best interests of the CEO and the organization.
  • A demonstrated commitment to Mozilla Foundation’s mission and to building an open, accessible and trustworthy internet.
  • The ability to work across time zones and occasionally outside standard working hours for Board meetings, major events or urgent organizational needs.
  • Comfortable traveling for Board meetings, leadership gatherings and major events.

We Are Excited To See Any Additional Experience With:

  • Senior roles in nonprofit, philanthropic, technology or public-interest organizations.
  • Supporting or advising investment, grantmaking or funding committees.

How We Work

A few things that are true about how we work at Mozilla Foundation. Here's a summary along with our expectation of how these should show up in this role:

  • Move toward the hard thing: you surface conflicts in priorities, resources or attention early, and give the CEO and executives direct, actionable input, including what they may not want to hear. You disagree constructively in the room, not afterward, and you don’t wait for someone else to raise it.
  • Stay curious and current: you stay close to what executives are seeing and what’s happening in our fields and communities, and turn it into the context the CEO needs. You pressure-test assumptions, including your own.
  • Work in the open: you document decisions and the reasoning behind them, so executives and teams can follow how and why priorities are set. You favor shared channels over side conversations wherever appropriate.
  • Focus and finish: you keep the CEO’s agenda focused on what matters most, make deliberate choices about what does and doesn’t need the CEO, and make sure decisions and commitments are seen through.
  • Flex with purpose: you move between long-term priorities and time-sensitive issues as context shifts, and adapt how you work with each executive. Flexibility isn’t about being agreeable; it’s staying responsive while holding to the mission and the CEO’s priorities.
  • Lead with care: you hold a high bar for the work while treating people as whole humans. You extend good faith to fellow executives, respect that each owns their area, and talk directly to the person who can solve the problem.

Salary and Benefits Information

Mozilla Foundation is dedicated to fair and equitable compensation for our staff. We aim to pay a competitive and market-based salary based on the responsibilities and requirements of the role. We do not ask for, or take into account, salary histories in our offer process.

The starting salary ranges for this role are listed below. 

  • Germany: €206,448.00 – €232,253.22
  • UK: £181,764.00 – £204,483.81
  • Canada: $356,400.00 – $400,948.65
  • US: $264,000.00 – $296,999.00

We also offer the following benefits:

  • Private Medical Insurance
  • Extended Sick Leave
  • Global Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Retirement Plan contributions
  • Paid Time Off: 20 days annual leave + sick days and your birthday
  • Company Holidays + EOY Shutdown
  • Wellness budget
  • Professional Development budget
  • Top up program for Pregnancy and Parental leaves

Benefits are subject to change at any time at the discretion of Mozilla Foundation.

Mozilla Foundation Hiring Practices

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities and expressions.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

title: Cloud Engineer - Quantum Computing (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Quantum computing is a new computing paradigm rapidly approaching commercial viability. Our unique approach combines laser-cooled trapped ions with microwave control and tailored magnetic fields. Our next-generation computing machines under development will be able to find solutions to problems that are out of reach today, thus enabling new innovative products and services for a brighter future.

We are looking for a Cloud Engineer (m/f/d) to join us in Hamburg or Siegen and build and operate the scalable, secure cloud platform that connects users with our trapped-ion quantum computers.

Responsibilities:

You will join our Quantum firmware Team as a Cloud Engineer. You will build the layer through which the world reaches our quantum computers. Users submit quantum programs; your services compile, schedule, and dispatch them to our machines and return the results:

  • Build and operate the cloud services that let users submit quantum programs to our systems and retrieve their results.

  • Develop and deploy our compilation pipeline as a scalable cloud service , from circuit input through transpilation down to hardware-level instructions

  • Design and maintain the public API and SDK entry points to our platform

  • Implement job queuing, scheduling, and dispatch towards the hardware backends, including quota, prioritisation, and result handling

  • Own authentication and authorisation across the platform: user and tenant identity, API keys and tokens, and role-based access to machines, jobs, and results, built on an established identity provider rather than from scratch

  • Guarantee tenant isolation, so that quantum programs and results are never visible across customer boundaries, and manage secrets and credentials across the stack

  • Work with the quantum firmware and hardware teams on the interfaces between cloud services and the machine itself

  • Instrument the platform for observability and keep an eye on latency, throughput, and cost

title: Cloud Native Security Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Report To: Delivery Manager

Job Location: Remote and/or London (right to work in UK or EU required)      

Employment Status: Full Time

Salary: Up to £85,000 + Benefits

Who is ControlPlane?

ControlPlane is a London headquartered consultancy specialising in cloud-native, Kubernetes, and open source solutions. Our expertise lies in helping organisations adopt and secure complex cloud infrastructures by implementing security measures that are "secure-by-design" and "secure-by-default." This engineering excellence has driven ControlPlane deeper into cybersecurity providing services like threat modelling, penetration testing, and supply chain security to ensure robust protection against cyberattacks in containerised and cloud-native environments.

We are acclaimed for our contributions to securing highly regulated industries, such as finance, healthcare, and national infrastructure. We help businesses improve their security posture through services like DevSecOps consulting, zero-trust architectures, and platform engineering. ControlPlane also focuses on advancing best practices in the Kubernetes ecosystem, offering specialised training and community engagement.

Our clients range from multinational banks to tech giants and public clouds, where we assist with both security and operational needs. In addition to consulting, we are active in the open source community, supporting projects like Flux CD and providing security tools for Kubernetes environments.

Over the coming years you’ll see us retain our focus on solving difficult problems for clients with intense security controls using pragmatic, real world solutions. Taking our extensive R&D to help organisations consume next generation and open source projects safely and securely - that might be extending our work with FINOS AI Readiness or the overhaul of open source supply chain security.

What We're Looking For in a Cloud Native Security Consultant

We are looking for Cloud Native Security consultants to represent the technical and cultural values of ControlPlane, leading our customers by example in the complex and fast-changing world of cloud native technology. You will perform a mix of client consulting, working on internal labs projects, and contributing to Open Source projects on ControlPlane’s behalf. 

There is no perfect candidate for this role. As we look to extend our cloud native security team we welcome engineers and architects with a diverse range of capabilities, experiences and backgrounds.

We are SANS authors (SEC584) and believe strongly in team learning and collaboration. Candidates with an aptitude to learn are preferred, and we provide full training for the newest cloud technologies that our customers rely on.

This is a unique job role within a successful start-up company where you will have the chance to make a positive impact, learn, grow and work with great colleagues who consistently challenge the status quo.

Roles, Responsibilities and Requirements of Our Cloud Native Security Consultant:

  • Knowledge of Threat Modelling and Cloud Native Security architectures (AWS, GCP, Azure)
  • Kubernetes and container experience (some of EKS, GKE, AKS, OpenShift, and container runtimes)
  • Knowledge of software supply chain security
  • DevSecOps principles and Engineering practices
  • CI/CD experience, automating security tests, and hardening pipelines 
  • Knowledge of security tooling from enterprise tools such as Aqua, Prisma, Sysdig, Lacework, etc to Open Source tools such as falco, kube-hunter, and kube-bench.
  • Knowledge and experience using hardening guides, compliance and risk management standards

A desire to learn, or experience with:

  • CLI tooling in any of the above technologies.
  • Golang or Python
  • Terraform and cloud infrastructure best practices (IaC, regulated systems)

Benefits

ControlPlane is a dynamic, cutting edge and passionate business for which to work. Our employees are the heart of our business, which means we care about our company culture and our employees’ wellbeing and progression. Alongside this, as our colleague you will have the following benefits:

  • Generous and competitive salary
  • Bonus
  • 33 days of paid holiday, including paid leave for the standard 8 UK Bank Holidays 
  • Enhanced Parental Leave
  • Private Medical insurance
  • An individual training budget for personal development, including but not limited to:
    • Conferences
    • Training (books, courses, coaching, as well as internal training which is of course included beyond budget)
    • Qualifications

We believe our peers are equally as important as the technology we use. We’re looking for people of the highest personal calibre, quietly confident, with a good work ethic, keenness to learn, emotional maturity and respect, who know that “we” is more than “me”, and who embrace human diversity of all kinds. As we grow you will help us to build a company culture of which we can all be proud. If you espouse these values, we want you!

title: Commercial Contracts Associate (NDA)
descriptionHtml:
About Norm Ai
Norm Ai, the agentic law company, has a client base with a combined $30 trillion in assets under management.


Norm Ai pioneered Legal Engineering, the process that empowers lawyers to build and supervise domain-specific AI agents with Norm’s proprietary suite of no-code software tools. Norm Ai technology is deployed inside many of the largest and most consequential institutions in the world.


Norm Ai is also the technology behind Norm Law, LLP, a separate but affiliated AI-native law firm built for the era of agentic AI. Norm Law’s attorneys advise leading institutions across private funds, private equity, venture capital, real estate, registered funds, and financial regulation, using the same legal intelligence platform that powers Norm Ai’s products.

AI Fluency:
Norm Ai prefers all team members to be fluent in AI. Successful candidates actively use AI in their day-to-day work to support thinking, creation, and problem-solving. They use it to improve the quality and speed of their work and to continuously refine how work gets done end-to-end.

Candidates should be prepared to demonstrate and discuss their AI usage throughout the interview process, including concrete examples of tools, workflows, and outcomes. We look for practical, hands-on experience, not theoretical familiarity.

This Role

As a Commercial Contracts Associate (NDA), you will work on a high impact team that provides important services to Norm Law’s clients, while using AI agents to streamline the drafting, review, and execution process in providing non-disclosure agreement review for clients. You’ll collaborate closely with partners, clients, and technology teams to deliver efficient, precise, and data-driven legal services for in-house legal teams of leading asset managers.

Our practice embraces the use of AI to reduce burden and increase your ability to focus on strategic legal judgment and client engagement.

What You'll Do

  • Document Drafting, Review, and Negotiation: Leverage AI agents to generate, compare, negotiate, and redline NDAs tailored to client guidelines

  • Incorporating Legal Context: Advise clients on their NDA playbooks and market standards, including ensuring AI agents understand each client's specific context and comparing client’s actual practices with playbook positions in order to guide updates.

  • Client Advisory: Partner with clients to demonstrate how AI-assisted workflows improve accuracy, transparency, and velocity.

What We're Looking For

  • Qualified solicitor admitted in England and Wales, with a current Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) practising certificate.

  • Strong drafting and communication skills; meticulous attention to detail.

  • Interest in applying technology to enhance traditional deal workflows.

What Success Looks Like

  • 30 Days: Learn firm AI platforms; begin supporting the commercial contracts team using AI-enabled review and drafting.

  • 60 Days: Independently manage discrete components of NDA review with AI support.

  • 90 Days: Lead AI-augmented workstreams in live NDA reviews, improving efficiency and accuracy in document management and execution processes.

Benefits

Benefits: pension plan with an employer contribution, medical and dental insurance coverage, employee referral bonus program, initial 2 week onboarding in the US.

Work Location

Location: Central London

Work model: Hybrid

In-office expectation: 4-5 days per week

Why Join Norm Law

You’ll be part of the founding UK team bringing a proven US category leader to a receptive UK market. You’ll have autonomy, visibility, and the opportunity to build meaningful relationships — backed by a world-class product, an experienced executive team, and a growing global reputation.

title: Commercial Lead UK
descriptionHtml:
About Klim

The team at Klim is building the operating system for regenerative agriculture. We help farms restore their soil - and turn that into real, measurable business value for the food companies, banks and insurers who depend on it.

We’re a Berlin-based agritech startup backed by $22M in Series A funding, partnering with global food leaders such as Nestlé and ADM to build supply chain resilience through regenerative agriculture. Since 2020, we’ve supported +4,000 farmers managing over 900,000 hectares.

Join our incredible team of 80+ dedicated people across Germany, the UK, Poland and Czechia to help build a more sustainable, resilient food system and drive real climate impact.

Your mission

As our Commercial Lead, you will be responsible for growing Klim's business in the UK. You'll source, win and expand partnerships with a wide variety of food companies operating in the UK, helping them build more profitable, resilient supply chains, and scale Klim’s business in a key strategic market.

You'll build our UK sales pipeline and help grow our presence in the market with a focus on generating leads, scoping consultative programmes, negotiating partnerships and managing key customer relationships.

You'll also play a leading role in identifying market opportunities, customer needs and emerging trends that can inform Klim’s UK strategy, go-to-market engine, marketing, and product roadmap.

This role is based in the UK, and we have a coworking space in London where the team meets to collaborate. Expect mostly UK-based travel, with occasional trips to our Berlin office for company-wide get-togethers.

What you'll do:

  • Shape our UK go-to-market strategy: define target accounts, account plans and pricing within Klim’s standard offering. Help lead our marketing and communications strategy, build our brand and reputation, and bring customer feedback into product and strategy.

  • Own the end-to-end enterprise sales cycle: guide CPGs, retailers, agri-traders and other businesses from outreach, discovery and qualification through to programme design, proposals, negotiation and signed contracts. Help stakeholders across finance, procurement and sustainability understand how soil regeneration supports Scope 3 reduction, supply chain resilience, lower sourcing risk and enterprise value.

  • Build UK partnerships: develop relationships with complementary businesses, grain traders, agronomy businesses and industry bodies that connect Klim with UK farmers and buyers.

  • Grow lasting customer relationships: develop initial programmes into larger, multi-year partnerships across commodities and sourcing regions. Collaborate with our internal teams to deliver successful programmes and support renewals.

  • Turn market insights into action: stay up to date with regulatory developments, competitors, industry trends and standards. Use this knowledge to advise customers and identify opportunities for Klim’s UK business.

You’ll be responsible for UK new business and account growth, reporting directly to Rory Davidson, UK Country Lead & Head of Marketing.

What success looks like after 12 months:

  • Revenue targets met: Target of net new UK contract value closed.

  • Pipeline targets met: a qualified UK pipeline target met, implementing a MEDDPICC sales motion

  • Expansion targets met: top UK accounts grown into larger or multi-year programmes.

  • New logos: Target of net new UK enterprise clients signed from our target ICPs

  • Market presence & reputation: Klim recognised as a credible voice on regenerative supply chains by UK buyers, partners & industry bodies


What you bring -

Must have:

You’re deeply motivated to grow Klim’s business in the UK and take it to the next level.

  • Location: You are based in the UK and have the right to work there.

  • Consulting or Enterprise sales: You have 5+ years in consulting and/or enterprise B2B sales, business development or client-facing leadership roles. You have a track record of scoping and leading large complex projects, and / or closing complex, 6- and 7-figure deals with a technical element (preferably within sustainability or procurement)

  • P&L Impact: Demonstrated experience developing and closing commercial partnerships, contracts, or other revenue-generating opportunities.

  • Sector depth: You have experience in the UK agri-food system - e.g. agri-food sustainability, agritech, soil carbon or MRV, agronomy & inputs, or food & drink supply chains.

  • Consultative approach: you diagnose before you pitch, build the business case together with the customer, and are comfortable managing different stakeholders - including senior finance and procurement leaders. Consulting experience is preferred.

  • Sales discipline: Experience with a structured sales method such as MEDDPIC, and CRM tools such as Pipedrive.

title: Compliance Director
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Compliance Director and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

  • Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

  • Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

  • Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

  • Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

  • Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

  • File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

  • Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

  • Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

  • Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

  • Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

  • Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

  • Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

  • Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

  • Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

  • Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

  • Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

  • Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

  • Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

  • Knowledge of Lithuanian AML law and Bank of Lithuania instructions.

  • Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

  • CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • People who copy policies from templates without fitting them to the business.

  • People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

Location

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.

title: Consultant(e) Intégration Paie
descriptionHtml:
Alassio recrute son ou sa Consultant(e) Intégration Paie !

En un coup d'œil

  • Contrat : CDI

  • Lieu : Paris ou Aix-en-Provence ; hybride, avec des déplacements ponctuels chez nos cabinets partenaires

  • Équipe : Déploiement & Accompagnement (DnA)

  • Expérience : 3 ans minimum en paie

  

Missions

 

🏗️ Alassio, en quelques mots

Le marché de la paie en cabinet d'expertise comptable est dominé depuis des décennies par des solutions historiques. Chez Alassio, notre ambition est de rénover le métier au bénéfice des gestionnaires de paie, avec un logiciel moderne, évolutif et pensé pour les réalités du terrain.

Lancé en juillet 2025 et déployé en clientèle depuis mars 2026, Alassio a levé 2,6 M€ en pre-seed auprès de Partech et de business angels de référence. Nous accélérons pour accompagner de nouveaux cabinets partout en France, tout en maintenant une exigence forte sur la qualité du produit et de l'accompagnement.

 

🎯 Pourquoi ce poste, maintenant

Changer de logiciel de paie est un projet lourd pour un cabinet. La réussite de chaque migration est décisive : c'est elle qui fait d'un cabinet signé un cabinet convaincu, puis un ambassadeur. Pour accompagner l'arrivée de nouveaux cabinets, nous renforçons l'équipe Déploiement & Accompagnement (DnA), qui assure un suivi actif de chacun de nos cabinets partenaires.

Ce poste est le premier recrutement de l’équipe DnA. Le playbook de migration, les supports de formation et les indicateurs de suivi se construisent avec les cabinets que tu accompagnes, et c’est toi qui les feras évoluer. Concrètement, cela veut dire de l’autonomie et de l’influence réelles dès les premiers mois.

 

🚀 Ton rôle

Tu accompagnes nos cabinets partenaires dans leur migration vers Alassio, de la formation à la mise en production, et tu incarnes la qualité de service d'Alassio auprès des équipes de gestionnaires de paie sur le terrain.

C'est un poste à la fois de pilotage et de terrain : en lien avec les équipes Sales et Product, tu mènes le projet de migration du cabinet, tu assures la formation initiale de ses gestionnaires de paie et tu animes les points de suivi tout au long de la phase pilote et des premiers mois de production.

 

🧩 Les étapes d'un déploiement

  1. Cadrage : kick-off structuré avec le cabinet, ateliers de recueil des besoins (conventions, spécificités des dossiers, reprise d'historique), planning partagé

  2. Pilote : formation initiale des gestionnaires de paie, migration d'un premier échantillon de dossiers, paies en parallèle et contrôle des écarts

  3. Déploiement : bascule progressive de dossiers supplémentaires selon le planning défini en amont, mise en production

  4. Suivi actif : accompagnement renforcé après le démarrage, puis passage de relais à l'équipe Support

 

🧭 Tes missions

  • Piloter le déploiement d'un portefeuille de 5 à 10 cabinets selon leur taille

  • Être l'interlocuteur de référence du responsable social du cabinet et de ses gestionnaires de paie ; animer les points d'étape et un bilan régulier avec chaque cabinet

  • Former les équipes : formation initiale des gestionnaires de paie, sessions de prise en main, approfondissements

  • Suivre la migration : reprise des données et des historiques, paramétrage des dossiers avec l'Ingénieur(e) Paramétrage Paie, paies en parallèle et contrôle des écarts

  • Coordonner les équipes internes mobilisées sur le cabinet : Sales, paramétrage, support, produit

  • Construire et faire évoluer le playbook de migration : étapes, checklists, supports de formation, indicateurs de suivi

  • Faire remonter au Product les besoins et les irritants observés sur le terrain

 

📊 Indicateurs de réussite

  • Satisfaction des cabinets de ton portefeuille

  • Respect du planning de déploiement

  • Rapidité de résolution des demandes, en lien avec les autres équipes d'Alassio

  • Adoption d'Alassio par les gestionnaires de paie du cabinet

 

🤝 Ton environnement

  • Rattachement : Alexandre (Responsable Déploiement & Accompagnement), au sein de l'équipe DnA

  • Tu travailles en lien étroit avec l'équipe Sales et l'équipe Métier

  • Outils : Alassio, Notion, Qualiobee

 

🗓️ Tes 6 premiers mois

  • À 1 mois : tu maîtrises l'outil et le playbook de migration, et tu co-pilotes un premier déploiement en binôme

  • À 3 mois : tu pilotes en autonomie tes premiers cabinets et tu contribues à l'amélioration du processus d'onboarding des cabinets

  • À 6 mois : tu gères un portefeuille complet de 5 à 10 cabinets, dont tu mènes entièrement le déploiement sur Alassio

  

Profil recherché

 

🌱 Expérience

Indispensable :

  • Formation en paie (BTS, licence pro, master ou titre professionnel Gestionnaire de paie) ou Bac+3 en RH

  • Au moins 3 ans d'expérience en paie, en cabinet d'expertise comptable ou chez un éditeur

  • Pratique d'un logiciel de paie du marché

  • Une expérience de migration de logiciel de paie ou de projet de déploiement

  • De l'aisance dans l'animation de formations

  • Sens de l'organisation et de la gestion de projet ; excellent relationnel, y compris avec des décisionnaires

  • Mobilité pour des déplacements ponctuels chez nos cabinets partenaires

Un plus :

  • Expérience de consultant(e) chez un éditeur de paie

  • Bonne connaissance de la DSN et des environnements multi-conventions

  • Expérience de conception de supports de formation

 

💎 Qualités

  • Une posture de conseil, adaptable au contexte de chaque cabinet

  • La pédagogie, la rigueur et le sens du suivi

  • Le calme et la fiabilité dans les moments sensibles d'une mise en production et lors des pics d'activité (clôtures de paie, mois de janvier)

  • Le goût de construire : tu es à l’aise dans une équipe resserrée, où les process s’écrivent en même temps qu’on les utilise

  

Processus de sélection

1️⃣ Appel d'introduction avec Alexandre (Responsable Déploiement & Accompagnement) ou Hector (COO) : 30 min

2️⃣ Entretien métier avec Alexandre et Huy Anh (Resp. Métier) : 45 min

3️⃣ Mise en situation en direct avec Alexandre et Hector : 1 h

4️⃣ Rencontre informelle avec l'équipe : 1 h

👉 Le processus se termine par des prises de référence.

  

Ce que nous offrons

 

👊 Une mission unique

Être le visage d'Alassio auprès de nos cabinets partenaires et construire la méthode de migration d'un logiciel qui change le quotidien des gestionnaires de paie.

 

🎁 Rémunération et avantages

  • 💰 Rémunération fixe de 45 à 55K€ selon l'expérience (hors primes) + BSPCE

  • 🏥 Mutuelle Alan

  • 🍽️ Carte Swile (titres-restaurant)

  • 💻 Matériel informatique haut de gamme (MacOS, écran incurvé)

  • 🏡 Télétravail régulier possible

  • 🤓 Offsites d'équipe réguliers (un par trimestre en moyenne)

 

Certaines personnes hésitent à postuler quand elles ne cochent pas toutes les cases. Si tu hésites, postule quand même : on en parlera volontiers.

 

➡️ Prochaines étapes

Si la mission te parle, postule via le formulaire de candidature. Pour toute question, écris à Pour en savoir plus sur Alassio : alassio.fr

title: Conversion Manager - Financial Services
descriptionHtml:
Why This Role Exists

At Pennylane, our website plays a pivotal role in acquiring and converting customers, transforming traffic from paid acquisition, SEO, partnerships, and other channels into sign-ups, demo bookings, and product adoption.

 

As we accelerate our Financial Services offering, including pro account, and the monetization of our existing customer base, we are seeking a Conversion Manager to own conversion across these strategic areas.

 

You will lead the production and optimization of website pages and paid landing pages, from identifying friction to measuring business impact.

 

You will join the Website team within Growth and collaborate closely with Growth Engineers and Data in a multidisciplinary squad.

 

🌍 About Pennylane

Pennylane is one of France’s leading fintech unicorns, building the financial and accounting operating system for European SMEs and accounting firms.

 

Founded in 2020, we help business owners make better decisions and empower accountants to focus on advising their clients.

 

Key Figures and Ambition

  • 💻 Over 1.3 million SMEs already work with Pennylane

  • 🤝 More than 7,000 accounting firms use our platform

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Over 1,100 Pennylaners from more than 25 nationalities

  • 💰 More than €400 million raised since launch

  • 🌍 Remote-friendly, international culture expanding across Europe

 

What You’ll Do

You will own conversion across the Financial Services and Monetization scope, working across website pages, paid landing pages, product journeys, experimentation, and measurement.

 

Own CRO and Experimentation

  • Define and execute the conversion strategy for key journeys, including pro account landing pages, pricing and product pages, demo-booking journeys, self-sign-up, and upsell flows

  • Build and run a continuous A/B testing program, from ideation and scoping to sizing, analysis, and ship-or-kill decisions

  • Identify conversion friction and opportunities through analytics and behavioral insights

  • Develop clear hypotheses based on user behavior, business priorities, and funnel performance

  • Ensure experiments are measured against meaningful business outcomes

 

Manage the Website Conversion Roadmap

  • Own and prioritize the conversion roadmap for your scope based on expected impact and feasibility

  • Turn opportunities into actionable briefs, specifications, and delivery plans

  • Work closely with Growth Engineers, Data, Design, and other stakeholders to ship improvements

  • Coordinate QA, launch, and post-launch analysis

  • Own key Financial Services journeys, including pro account activation and the accountant portal

  • Contribute to monetization journeys such as upsell and self-sign-up

 

Build and Optimize Paid Landing Pages

  • Produce and optimize landing pages for Financial Services and Monetization campaigns

  • Help increase the speed and volume of landing-page delivery, removing the current bottleneck

  • Partner with Demand Generation and Paid/SEA teams to translate campaign objectives into high-performing pages

  • Develop a strong understanding of target audiences, market context, and local messaging

  • Use these insights to improve both paid landing pages and the wider website experience

 

Own Measurement and Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Define instrumentation and tracking plans with Data

  • Build and maintain dashboards to monitor conversion performance

  • Report on results, learnings, and next steps to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Work closely with Demand Gen, Product, Sales and Customer Success Operations, Brand, Design, and Engineering

  • Create alignment across teams and move projects forward without relying on formal authority

 

What You Bring

  • 3–5 years of experience in CRO, Conversion, Website Product Management, Growth, or a related field

  • Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, digital products, or another data-driven environment

  • A track record of shipping initiatives end-to-end and demonstrating their impact on business metrics

  • Strong hands-on experience with analytics and CRO tools, such as Amplitude and Contentsquare

  • Ability to independently analyse data, identify patterns, and formulate relevant hypotheses

  • Solid understanding of A/B testing methodology, including experiment sizing, success metrics, statistical pitfalls, and decision-making

  • Experience managing a roadmap and prioritizing initiatives based on impact and feasibility

  • Strong project management skills, from writing a clear brief to coordinating delivery and measuring results

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to:

    • Write clear briefs for designers and engineers

    • Explain prioritization decisions to stakeholders

    • Present results and recommendations to non-technical audiences

  • Ability to build relationships and secure alignment across multiple teams

  • Fluent French and professional English

 

🛠️ Tools and Environment

You will work with tools and processes dedicated to experimentation, analytics, behavioral analysis, tracking, and landing-page production.

 

Our Tools Include

  • Amplitude

  • Contentsquare

  • A/B testing and experimentation platforms

  • Analytics and reporting dashboards

  • Website content and landing-page production tools

 

You will collaborate closely with Growth Engineers, Data, Demand Generation, Product, Sales and Customer Success Operations, Brand, and Design.

 

What You Can Expect

  • Ownership of conversion across two strategic areas for Pennylane: Financial Services and Monetization

  • Direct and measurable impact on sign-ups, demo bookings, product activation, and upsell performance

  • The opportunity to shape the conversion roadmap across website and paid landing pages

  • A central role in structuring and scaling our experimentation program

  • Close collaboration with Growth Engineering, Data, Product, Demand Gen, Sales, Customer Success Operations, Brand, and Design

  • High level of autonomy and visibility across the organization

  • Challenging and supportive environment focused on ownership, execution, learning, and measurable impact

 

Success in This Role

Your success will be measured by:

 

  • The frequency and quality of experiments launched

  • The speed and volume of website and landing-page delivery

  • Conversion-rate improvement across the Financial Services and Monetization funnels

  • Growth in relevant outcomes, including sign-ups and demo bookings

  • Ability to absorb inbound landing-page demand without creating a delivery bottleneck

  • Quality of tracking, reporting, and learnings shared with stakeholders

 

📍 Location & Working Model

Permanent position based in Paris on a hybrid basis or fully remote anywhere in France.

 

🌈 Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

Pennylane is dedicated to fostering an inclusive and supportive workplace, providing equal opportunities for all candidates, regardless of background, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other characteristic.

 

If you’re excited about this role and think you could make an impact, we encourage you to apply—even if you don’t meet every requirement.
