descriptionHtml:
Founding Engineer


Role can be based remotely in the EEA or hybrid in our London or Munich offices.

Fixed software is the wrong shape for logistics, because every team runs its processes differently. Tare is our solution. Combining agentic AI with deterministic logic means Tare fits to any customer but runs the same way every single time. We have just closed our pre-seed funding round with a top European VC and we are now looking for a founding engineer to build Tare with us.

About Tarebase

We're Dom and Felix, the two co-founders of Tarebase. Dom is a former SVP at a global unicorn, overseeing tens of millions in global carrier spend, with deep logistics domain experience from Amazon, Nestle and EY. Felix was a founding engineer at Raycast and has spent more than two decades building software systems. We've raised pre-seed funding from a top-tier European VC and are building our MVP together with early design partners, who will become our first customers. As our first employee, you'd have a real say in both the product and the engineering decisions behind it.

Logistics is difficult to run well, and experienced people are hard to hire. Smaller businesses often pay too much for shipping, struggle to give customers a good delivery experience, and can't match larger competitors' technology or hiring budgets. The software available to them is often expensive, dated or too cumbersome. We want to make logistics less of a burden so these businesses can spend more time selling their products.They're the customers we want to build for: Europe alone has around 26 million SMEs, employing more than 100 million people.

Just putting a chat interface and GPT-wrapper on top of the problem is not what we're building. We're combining extraction and analysis, workflow automation, agentic and compiled AI with deterministic, verifiable logic. Recent advances in AI make more of this possible, but building a system that does it reliably is still hard. We're looking for someone who wants to advance the state of the art in this area with us.

About you

The description below is an ideal, not a checklist. If you don't tick every box but feel ready for the challenges of being the first engineer at an early-stage startup, we'd still like to hear from you. What matters most to us is that you're motivated, committed, willing to stick with hard problems, and someone we can count on.

You have a strong technical background and a track record of building and shipping software systems, whether that's cloud backends, web applications, AI-supported systems or a mix of these. You enjoy working across engineering and product. You think like a product engineer: you care about UX/UI, and you want direct contact with customers and the people who use what you build.

You'll work mostly in Rust and TypeScript, across the full stack: data engineering, AI, backend, frontend, infrastructure and deployment. We especially value experience with either language from before AI coding tools and a solid understanding of its ecosystem so you can make considered choices. We also value experience operating distributed systems and data-intensive systems in the cloud, including multi-tenant environments and the scaling and security challenges they bring, databases, and durable execution runtimes.

You use coding agents effectively, but stay close to the code. You know their limitations in a large codebase, review and challenge their work, and take testing, debugging, refactoring and documentation seriously. You can design useful tests and evaluations, manage complexity, and tell when something is genuinely ready to ship.

You also enjoy digging into challenging problems. You keep up with what current models, agent harnesses and research make possible, and you can judge what actually works for a given use case. You know how to build agents and AI workflows into a product and use evaluations, validation and deterministic logic to make what they produce consistent and verifiable. You're comfortable extracting structure from messy documents and care a lot about data quality. You experiment, measure the results, question your assumptions, and keep going until you've found a solution that really holds up.

You can turn that work into shipped software, taking a product idea or technical direction through design and implementation without waiting for someone to assign you a ticket. We work remotely, so clear communication and follow-through matter a lot to us. We value people who manage their own work, can be counted on, and raise important issues early.

How to apply

Apply with the button on this page.

Please ensure to use a hand-written CV. We read every application ourselves. It's fine to use tools for spelling or translation, but we want to hear your voice.

Our process

The process should take a few weeks from start to finish depending on your availability.

  1. Application review. If we love your resume we will send over some short questions.

  2. Intro call with Dom and Felix. An informal conversation about the role, the technology and what you're looking for.

  3. Technical deep dive with Felix. We talk briefly about a system you’ve worked on (no need to share anything confidential), then work through a system design problem together.

  4. Half a day with us in Munich or London. We cover your travel, hotel if needed, and meals. You spend about two hours on a made-up task similar to the problems we work on, using your usual tools and coding agents. Then we have lunch, go through your work together, and talk through a customer scenario.

  5. References and offer. We speak with 1-2 people you've worked with (only with your agreement) and aim to decide within 48 hours.

If we don't move forward after the technical conversation or later, we'll share some feedback with you.

Compensation: €100.000–120.000 base salary plus 0.75–1% equity

Setup: A MacBook Pro and whatever else you need to work well. If you'd rather not work from home, we'll pay for a coworking space near you.

Location: Munich or London, or remote within Europe (GMT-1 to GMT+3) with regular meet-ups.

title: Founding GTM
descriptionHtml:
Company

Neuphonic is building the future of on-device voice AI.

 

We develop ultra-low-latency voice models that enable super-realistic, human-like speech directly on devices. Our focus is on building efficient generative audio models and infrastructure that can run on CPU-constrained hardware, enabling real-time voice interaction without relying on large cloud infrastructure.

 

By dramatically reducing latency and compute requirements, we're making natural conversational AI possible on phones, embedded devices, browsers, and edge systems. This requires building high-performance systems that bridge machine learning, real-time audio processing, and distributed infrastructure.

 

Neuphonic was founded in April 2024 and has raised significant funding from leading European investors. We work with global enterprises across hardware and consumer AI that are building the next generation of voice-enabled products. Our open source models have been downloaded over 4 million times and earned over 6,500 GitHub stars since launch.

 

Our vision is a world where voice becomes the most natural interface for AI, enabling seamless, intuitive interactions that are accessible to everyone.

 

Role

We're looking for a Founding GTM Associate to build the top of our enterprise pipeline, working side by side with our founders and sales team.

 

Our go-to-market runs from open source to enterprise. Developers find and build on our open models, and the companies they work for need production-grade, supported versions for products where latency, privacy and offline operation matter. Your job is to make that path faster and more predictable.

 

This is a hands-on, commercial role with one clear goal: book as many qualified meetings as possible for our sales team. You'll report to the CEO and work directly with the founders, research team and sales team.

 

We are not looking for a marketer measured on impressions. We're looking for someone commercially sharp, comfortable reaching out to people, and technical enough to hold their own with engineers.

 

Your work will include:

  • Identifying which companies are using our open models, researching them, and getting the right ones into a conversation with sales

  • Running targeted outreach to engineering and product leaders at our target accounts, by email, LinkedIn and through our community

  • Booking meetings directly with prospects and handing them over to our account executives with clear context

  • Building target account lists for events, dinners and conferences, and following up within 48 hours after

  • Creating the assets that open doors: account research, tailored demos, one-pagers and case studies

  • Supporting open source launches and creator partnerships so they generate pipeline, not just attention

  • Tracking which channels produce meetings, and recommending where we put more time and budget

  • Helping build the GTM processes and playbooks we'll scale as the team grows

 

In your first few months, the priority is turning companies already using our models into meetings. Events, launches and creator partnerships grow from there. Open source is our biggest advantage, but we care about meetings, not channels. If paid, LinkedIn or outbound gets better results, we want you to prove it and run with it.

 

This is a role to learn fast in. You'll see how an enterprise AI company is built from the inside, and as our GTM team scales, there's a clear path for you to lead part of it.

 

You have:

  • 1–3 years' experience in sales development, B2B sales, consulting, a startup generalist role or another demanding commercial environment

  • Strong commercial instincts: you can spot which companies are worth our time, and explain why

  • Comfort reaching out to people you don't know, and following up until you get a response

  • Comfort testing new channels quickly and dropping what doesn't work

  • A proactive approach and comfort building from scratch

 

Bonus points for experience in AI, speech or edge computing, booking meetings for an enterprise sales team, or working in a CRM day to day.

 

This probably isn't the right role for you if you're looking for a marketing or brand role, or if you'd rather support deals than create them.

 

How we'll measure success:

Success means a reliable, growing flow of qualified enterprise meetings for our sales team.

 

We'll look at:

title: Founding ML Engineer (Spectrum)
descriptionHtml:
Software engineers and AI agents alike suffer from the same problem: finding that one person or place that will answer their tough, specific question. Many solutions promise to solve this with similarity search in vector databases. Unfortunately, finding the answer is often a puzzle with pieces to be collected across a myriad of contradictory sources and cannot be solved without surgical search and careful reasoning. 

Spectrum collects data from an organization’s code, docs, and issues, and organizes knowledge in a unified ontology that AI agents can efficiently search through and reason over. We aim to revolutionize the semantic layer space for software-building organizations and move beyond specs that fall out of sync with code, introducing a living spec – one that’s extracted from the whole system and used to keep it aligned. Spectrum is meant to be the single source of truth for all product and architectural knowledge.

Spectrum is a resident of JetBrains' startup incubator, with startup speed and autonomy, and backed by 25 years of developer tooling expertise. We are looking for a top-class ML Engineer who will help us shape the future of software development. You will own our AI and ML engineering stack and help define the research agenda for our team. Your technical vision and design decisions will directly shape the product and determine its success.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Designing and building the ML/LLM solution for data ingestion, knowledge extraction, retrieval, and subsequent reasoning.
  • Creating the datasets, metrics, and pipelines that drive measurable improvements across the system.
  • Architecting and improving agents for context retrieval, knowledge extraction, and data alignment, which includes prompt engineering, model selection, and inference optimization.
  • Establishing MLOps practices, including orchestration, observability, and experiment tracking.
  • Collaborating with the engineering team on system design and with JetBrains Research on the research agenda.
  • Defining hiring criteria, growing the ML team, and shaping the ML team culture.

We expect you to have:

  • A proven track record as an ML/AI Lead.
  • At least five years of experience in ML/AI systems, with at least two years focused on LLMs and generative AI.
  • A deep understanding of the LLM ecosystem, including model architectures and fine-tuning approaches.
  • Hands-on experience with:
    • Prompt engineering and LLM pipeline design, including evaluation.
    • Agentic frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangSmith, smolagents, or an equivalent.
    • Vector databases and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns.
    • Deploying and scaling LLM-powered applications using APIs (e.g. OpenAI or Anthropic) or open-source models.
  • Strong Python skills – Kotlin knowledge would be a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

Our ideal candidate would have:

  • Experience with ontologies, knowledge graphs, or graph-based reasoning.
  • Experience in early-stage startups – you enjoy the zero-to-one phase.
  • The ability to think strategically about product-led AI, beyond just training models in isolation.
  • A background in code analysis, developer tools, or software engineering research.
  • Experience with multi-agent systems or complex agentic workflows.
  • Actively contributed to relevant open-source projects or publications.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary and JetBrains benefits.
  • A generous runway and corporate resources with startup autonomy.

title: FPGA Firmware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Singular Photonics:

Singular Photonics is a fast-growing fabless semiconductor start-up, developing Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) sensors that bring advanced computation directly into imaging. Our sensors enable innovations across LiDAR, fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM), spectroscopy and time-resolved optical measurements, powering next-generation solutions for customers worldwide. Based at Orchard Brae House in Edinburgh, we are a close-knit team at the forefront of the photonics revolution.

About the Role:

We are seeking an FPGA Firmware Engineer to join our multidisciplinary R&D team. This is an FPGA role: you will design, implement and verify the Verilog firmware that powers our SPAD sensors, captures photon timing data at high rates and streams it to the host.

Our sensors generate data faster than most imaging systems ever see, so the interesting problems here are real ones: clock domain crossing, timing closure and getting data off the device without losing a photon. You will work alongside our hardware, ASIC and software engineers, from architecture through to system bring-up and customer deployment.

You will report to the Lead Firmware Engineer.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Architecture: Define FPGA requirements and architecture for SPAD sensor readout, in discussion with the hardware, ASIC and software teams.
  • RTL Design: Implement, verify and debug Verilog modules for data acquisition, photon timing, histogramming and sensor control.
  • Verification: Design and run simulations and testbenches, with coverage sufficient to trust the design before it reaches hardware.
  • Synthesis & Timing: Own synthesis, constraints, clock domain crossing and timing closure on AMD-Xilinx FPGA family devices in Vivado.
  • High-Speed Interfaces: Build and integrate the high-speed interfaces that move sensor data: PCIe, USB3, Ethernet, AXI interface, MIPI, LVDS, SLVS, Camera Link.
  • Bring-Up & Debug: Lead firmware bring-up on new boards and sensors, debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analysers and in-system probes.
  • Source Control & Build: Keep RTL under version control with a repeatable, automated build, and document designs to the standard our ISO 9001 design control process requires.
  • Reviews & Support: Contribute to design reviews, and support the software team and customers during field integration.

Experience & Skills:

Essential:

  • Strong proficiency in Verilog, and a solid grounding in RTL design, synthesis and timing closure.
  • Hands-on experience with AMD-Xilinx Vivado and its toolchain.
  • Experience writing your own testbenches and verifying a design in simulation before hardware.
  • Experience bringing up firmware on real hardware and debugging it in the lab.
  • Experience with at least one high-speed interface or bus at RTL level.
  • Comfortable in a small company where priorities shift and everyone pitches in.
  • Working with complex, existing codebases and seamlessly integrating new functionality with minimal disruption.

Desirable:

  • SystemVerilog, and verification practices beyond directed testbenches.
  • Comfortable working in Linux operating systems.
  • Exposure to any of PCIe, AXI interface, USB3, Ethernet, MIPI, LVDS, SLVS or Camera Link.
  • C, C++ or Python for embedded software integration and test automation.
  • Experience with image sensors, time-of-flight, TDCs or single-photon detection.
  • Familiarity with PCB design tools such as Altium Designer, and reading schematics during debug.

Educational Background:

  • Degree in Electronics Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2-5 years' experience in FPGA and digital design.

Key Attributes & Behaviours:

  • Rigour: Disciplined about verification - you would rather find it in simulation than on the bench.
  • Debugging: Systematic when the fault could be in the RTL, the board or the sensor, and comfortable with the instruments that tell you which.
  • Clarity: Writes documentation and code that colleagues can pick up without you in the room.
  • Collaboration: Works well across the hardware, ASIC and software boundaries rather than only inside the FPGA.
  • Ownership: Takes a problem from architecture through to a working system, and sees it through.
  • Adaptability: Comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment where the requirement can move.

Success Indicators:

  • Firmware that meets timing and functions correctly on first hardware more often than not, with issues found in simulation rather than on the bench.
  • Effective bring-up and debugging support during prototype validation and customer deployment, with hardware and firmware issues resolved promptly.
  • Design documentation, simulation coverage and design review contributions good enough for another engineer to maintain the work.

Benefits of Joining Singular Photonics

At Singular Photonics, we are committed to fostering a rewarding and supportive environment for our team. As an FPGA Firmware Engineer, you will benefit from:

  • Pension: 5% company contribution.
  • Share Options: Participation in the Company EMI Share Option Scheme, so you share in the growth you help build.
  • Enhanced Annual Leave: 35 days paid annual leave per year, inclusive of UK public holidays.
  • Hybrid Working: Primarily office-based, with flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week (full time worker).
  • Career Growth: Work on silicon and systems few engineers get near, with the chance to shape how we do FPGA development as the team grows.
  • Additional Benefits: [Cycle to work and private medical insurance (once implemented)

Why Join Us

This position offers a rare opportunity to work at the forefront of SPAD sensor technology, driving innovation and shaping future applications in photonics and imaging. At Singular Photonics you will be part of a passionate, close-knit team, where the work you do is visible in the product and in the hands of customers.

Location & Work Environment

Based at Orchard Brae House, Queensferry Road, Edinburgh. This is a full-time, permanent role. The work is hands-on with hardware in our lab, so it is primarily office-based, with flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week.

Right to work in the UK is essential. We are unfortunately unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities

Singular Photonics is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and make appointments on merit, regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

If you need any adjustments to the application or interview process, please let us know and we will do what we can to accommodate you.

title: Full stack engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Nabla

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

The best of AI at the service of healthcare

Nabla’s phenomenal traction is the result of 3 years of diligent product development.

Led by former Meta AI Research engineers, our team has consistently anticipated how AI can revolutionize healthcare delivery. Our Machine Learning team continually leverages the latest advancements to unlock AI’s full potential in healthcare.

Yann LeCun, Meta’s ex-Chief AI Scientist and Turing award winner, is an advisor to Nabla. He’s now focused on AMI Labs, with whom we have a close partnership.

Engineering at Nabla

Engineering at Nabla is lean, fast-moving, and deeply technical. Our teams span machine learning, native desktop applications, and platform infrastructure to deliver AI into clinical settings reliably and at scale.

Your team

At Nabla, product development is led jointly by Engineering and Product and organized into cross-functional squads, each focused on a specific product area. Squads bring together product managers, designers, engineers of different profiles, and domain experts, and operate with a high level of ownership.

As a Full-stack Engineer, you'll join one of these squads and contribute end to end to a specific part of the product.

The technical challenges

  • Volumetry and efficiency: We handle more than 2.5 million medical encounters per month. Each one is automatically turned into a clinical note sent to the clinician's patient record system, saving thousands of hours of administrative work and giving healthcare professionals more time for their patients.

  • Real-time audio transcription: capturing and streaming audio reliably, from in-person visits as well as video consultations, and turning it into transcripts with very low latency

  • Resilience: keeping the product working on weak or unstable networks, with no data lost and no disruption to the clinician

  • Healthcare integrations: building robust connections to the third-party medical systems clinicians already rely on.

  • Complex AI services: designing and running multi-stage LLM pipelines and agentic workflows at scale, with the reliability and auditability a clinical setting requires

These challenges come with demanding product requirements:

  • Zero friction: clinicians have no time to learn a new tool, so the product must be fast to set up, intuitive, and useful from the very first consultation

  • Trust: what we generate goes into patient records, so quality and reliability are non-negotiable

  • Works everywhere: web, desktop and mobile, in clinics, hospitals or remote consultations

Your impact

  • Build and improve product features across web, desktop and mobile platforms

  • Design and evolve the back-end APIs and services that power them

  • Collaborate closely with Product, ML, and Design to take projects from idea to production

  • Write clean, maintainable code and contribute to team best practices

  • Learn from senior engineers and grow your skills across the stack

Your DNA

  • Solid foundations in Computer Science

  • 4+ years of industry experience in full-stack engineering

  • Proficient in React (strong Vue.js experience also considered)

  • Proficient in at least one back-end language such as Java, Kotlin, Scala, C#/.NET, Go, or Rust. We use Kotlin internally, and it's fine if you haven't worked with it yet

  • Comfortable working with AI coding tools and agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, etc.), and keen to use AI in your day-to-day work

  • Curious, eager to learn, and motivated to grow in a fast-moving team

  • Care about code quality and maintainability

  • Enjoy working in an international team where English is our primary language

Our Stack

  • Frontend: TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, Rust, Electron

  • Backend: Kotlin / JVM, GraphQL, PostgreSQL

  • ML & Infra: Python, PyTorch, Slurm, GCP, Terraform, Kubernetes

Where you'll be based

Our offices are based in Paris 3e (Arts & Métiers)

Remote policy: 2 days a week

Possibility of working abroad remotely up to 2 weeks, once a year.

Benefits

Just like we’re dedicated to supporting doctors’ well-being, ensuring yours is a top priority. We firmly believe that by prioritizing your well-being, we support you to excel in your work.

Here are the benefits you get when joining Nabla:

  • Stock ownership

  • 100% healthcare coverage

  • Meal vouchers

  • Public transportation costs covered at 50%

  • Exercise class during the workday: Yoga, running, pilates, HIIT

  • Unlimited budget for book purchases, so you can continue to learn about ML / Healthcare

  • Culture of trust & accountability — your output matters more than your clock-in time

Life at Nabla

When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed.

We work hard and make time to have fun, too. Our #nablabla channel is just as active as #feature-show-off. We support well-being with workday activities at least three times a week; choose from yoga, running, Pilates, or HIIT. We also host regular off-sites, meet up across New York, Paris, San Francisco, and other cities, and keep the chocolate and nuts well stocked.

If this sounds like an environment where you’ll thrive, we look forward to reading your application.

Our Values at Nabla

Joining Nabla means being part of a team that shares a commitment to excellence, humility, growth, and inclusion.

Every day is a new chance to excel

We aim for nothing less than the best and are willing to put in the effort and dedication required to exceed standards. We learn from yesterday’s failures and do better every day.

Stay humble

There’s no place for ego in our team. Our collective success is more important than individual achievements. We see humility as wisdom — keeping focus on the bigger picture.

Feedback is a gift

We embrace feedback and foster a culture of trust and respect that helps everyone grow. We communicate openly about both achievements and challenges, and we actively involve each other in finding solutions.

Committed to diversity

We recognize the ongoing challenge of diversity in tech. Our responsibility starts with fostering an inclusive environment where everyone feels empowered to be their authentic selves and do their best work.

Diversity & Inclusion

Diversity and inclusivity are fundamental values at Nabla. We embrace individuals from various backgrounds, including race, gender, educational history, sexual orientation, and beyond.

As an equal opportunity employer, we actively seek out and welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds, believing that a wide range of perspectives enriches our team and enhances our ability to innovate and thrive.

Avoid recruitment scams: Stay safe and informed

There is an active employment and financial scam which uses Nabla to collect personal information. Deine Mission

Du entwickelst Anwendungen, die Menschen im Arbeitsalltag tatsächlich Arbeit abnehmen. Von der verständlichen Oberfläche über die Backend-Logik bis zur Anbindung bestehender Systeme.

Bei Agentur Philipp bauen wir KI-Lösungen und individuelle Software für den Mittelstand. Dafür suchen wir einen Fullstack Developer, der Anforderungen hinterfragt, technisch mitdenkt und Anwendungen zuverlässig in den produktiven Einsatz bringt.

Du arbeitest je nach Projekt mit unterschiedlichen Technologien: JavaScript und TypeScript im Frontend, PHP und Laravel, Node.js oder Python im Backend. Gemeinsam mit dem Team wählst du die passende Lösung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Webanwendungen vom Frontend bis zum Backend und begleitest sie bis zum produktiven Betrieb.

  • Du baust verständliche Benutzeroberflächen mit React, Next.js, Vue.js oder vergleichbaren Frameworks.

  • Du entwickelst Backends und APIs mit PHP und Laravel, Node.js oder Python und FastAPI, passend zu den Anforderungen des Projekts.

  • Du bindest bestehende Kunden-, ERP- und Drittsysteme an und sorgst für einen zuverlässigen Datenaustausch.

  • Du entwirfst Datenmodelle und setzt Geschäftslogik, Benutzerverwaltung, Rollen und Berechtigungen sauber um.

  • Du integrierst KI-Funktionen und automatisierte Workflows in unsere Anwendungen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unseren KI- und Automatisierungsentwicklern zusammen.

  • Du sorgst mit Tests, Logging und Fehlerbehandlung dafür, dass Anwendungen auch außerhalb des Idealfalls funktionieren.

  • Du entwickelst bestehende Systeme weiter und behältst Wartbarkeit, Sicherheit und Performance im Blick.

  • Du stimmst technische Anforderungen mit der Projektleitung ab und machst frühzeitig sichtbar, wenn etwas unklar ist oder aufwendiger wird.

  • Du dokumentierst wichtige technische Entscheidungen so, dass andere im Team deine Arbeit nachvollziehen und weiterführen können.

Das bringst du mit

  • Praktische Erfahrung darin, Webanwendungen eigenständig vom Frontend bis zum Backend zu entwickeln und produktiv einzusetzen.

  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in JavaScript und TypeScript sowie Erfahrung mit React, Next.js, Vue.js oder einem vergleichbaren Frontend-Framework.

  • Gute Kenntnisse in PHP und praktische Erfahrung mit Laravel.

  • Erfahrung mit Node.js oder Python, idealerweise mit einem Backend-Framework wie Express, NestJS oder FastAPI.

  • Sicherer Umgang mit relationalen Datenbanken wie MySQL oder PostgreSQL sowie Erfahrung mit Datenmodellierung und Datenbankmigrationen.

  • Erfahrung mit REST-APIs, Authentifizierung und der Integration externer Systeme.

  • Routine im Umgang mit Git, Docker und gängigen Deployment-Prozessen.

  • Gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sind Voraussetzung. Du kannst Anforderungen, technische Rückfragen und Abstimmungen im Team und mit unseren Kunden sicher auf Deutsch klären.

  • Du denkst an Berechtigungen, Datenschutz und Fehlerfälle, bevor die Anwendung beim Kunden läuft.

  • Du arbeitest dich in bestehende Codebasen und neue Technologien ein. Du musst nicht jedes genannte Framework beherrschen, solltest aber Frontend und Backend sicher abdecken.

  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, sprichst Probleme offen an und bringst übernommene Aufgaben zuverlässig zum Abschluss.

Das ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung mit LLM-APIs, RAG-Systemen oder anderen KI-Funktionen.

  • Erfahrung mit n8n oder vergleichbaren Automatisierungsplattformen.

  • Vertiefte Kenntnisse im Laravel-Ökosystem, beispielsweise Livewire oder Inertia.js.

  • Erfahrung mit ERP-Schnittstellen, Webhooks, Queues, Hintergrundjobs und asynchroner Verarbeitung.

  • Kenntnisse in CI/CD, Linux, Monitoring oder Cloud-Infrastruktur.

  • Erfahrung mit automatisierten Frontend-, Backend- und Integrationstests.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Anwendungen, die bei Kunden im Alltag eingesetzt werden. Du siehst, wofür du entwickelst und was deine Arbeit verändert.

  • Unterschiedliche Aufgaben rund um individuelle Software, KI-Kollegen, Schnittstellen und Prozessautomatisierung.

  • Ein breiter Tech-Stack und technische Entscheidungen, die sich am Projekt orientieren.

  • Technischer Gestaltungsspielraum und die Möglichkeit, unsere Entwicklungsstandards mit aufzubauen.

  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit KI-Entwicklern, Automatisierungsexperten und Projektleitung.

  • Direkter Austausch mit den Menschen, die Entscheidungen treffen. Kurze Wege und schnelle Umsetzung.

  • Remote-freundliches Arbeiten mit regelmäßigem persönlichem Austausch in Dingolfing. Für die finale Gesprächsrunde möchten wir dich vor Ort kennenlernen.

Über Agentur Philipp

Agentur Philipp ist eine KI-Umsetzungsberatung für den Mittelstand. Wir beraten nicht nur, sondern bauen Systeme, die im Alltag funktionieren, Aufwand reduzieren und einen messbaren Unterschied machen.

Unsere Haltung ist klar: Verstehen, Anpacken, Liefern und Besser werden.

Klingt nach dir?

Dann schick uns deinen Lebenslauf, GitHub-, Portfolio- oder Projektlinks und gern eine kurze Beschreibung einer Anwendung, die du selbst produktiv gebaut hast. Was war deine Verantwortung? Welche technische Entscheidung war besonders wichtig? Und wie hast du sichergestellt, dass die Anwendung im Alltag zuverlässig läuft?

Uns interessiert, was du gebaut hast und wie du an Probleme herangehst.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung.

title: General Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As General Manager of Doit Lithuania, you will build and run the business in Lithuania and grow it across the European Economic Area.

You will be the first senior hire in Lithuania. You will own the regulatory relationship, the build of the team, the partner network and the launch. You will sit on the management board and lead the business day to day.

We’re looking for a generalist who learns quickly, thinks deeply, and enjoys solving difficult problems in a fast-moving, regulated environment.

What You’ll Own

  • Own the relationship with the Bank of Lithuania and other regulators.

  • Build the Vilnius team, including compliance, operations and control functions.

  • Select and negotiate with execution, custody, fund and banking partners.

  • Own the business plan, financial projections, capital plan and budget.

  • Launch the investment platform in Lithuania and roll it out across the EEA.

  • Set up governance, policies and controls that meet EU and Lithuanian requirements.

  • Work with group leadership on product, engineering and growth.

  • Report to the board and take ownership of business and regulatory outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • Generalist background in consulting, investment banking, start-ups, private equity or venture capital.

  • Experience building or scaling a business, ideally in financial services or fintech.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and business judgment.

  • Ability to learn regulation quickly and work credibly with regulators.

  • Strong ownership and execution skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with boards, regulators, partners and teams.

  • Comfortable working across product, operations, finance and compliance.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a senior manager.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

  • Curious, resourceful, and driven to build.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania.

  • Experience with MiFID II, brokerage, wealth management or fund distribution.

  • Experience building or running a regulated financial business in the EU.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • Those who need fixed scope and slow timelines.

  • People who avoid messy cross-functional problems.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

  • People who see regulation as someone else’s problem.

Location

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.

title: Genesis-World: Core Simulation Engine Engineer
descriptionHtml:
What we’re building

Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.

Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.

Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.

This is at the core of Genesis AI’s strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.

Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.

You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.

The problems waiting for you

  • Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.

  • Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.

  • Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.

  • Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.

  • Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.

  • Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.

  • Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.

  • Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.

  • Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.

Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.

Who you are

You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design.

You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job.

  • Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc).

  • Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale.

  • Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants.

  • At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon)

  • Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community.

Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work.

For more information, visit WPP.com.

Why we're hiring:

As part of WPPs Elevate28 strategy, we are accelerating a major Finance Technology transformation to simplify, modernise and standardise the platforms, data and processes that underpin Global Finance. This portfolio is critical to statutory reporting, management reporting, forecasting, planning, control, performance management, compliance, and executive decision-making. 

The Global Programme Director - Finance Technology will shape, govern and drive WPP’s global Finance Technology transformation portfolio.   • Manage system integrators, software vendors and delivery partners against commitments, outcomes, commercial levers and performance expectations
  • Lead and coach programme directors, delivery leads, PMOs and matrixed teams to raise delivery standards, strengthen transparency and build a culture of accountability. 

What you'll need:

  • Proven track record of leading multi-year transformation portfolios with significant budgets, multiple delivery partners, complex governance and senior executive sponsorship.

title: Global Service Specialist - Semiconductor Equipment (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
Description

Our quantum sensing technology is already operating in customer environments across United States, Asia and Europe. As our installed base grows and we move from first deployments to repeat orders, ensuring the reliability and performance of every system becomes increasingly important.

As our Global Service Specialist, based at our Munich HQ, you’ll be part of a rapid-deployment team that resolves complex and escalated technical issues across our worldwide installed base. You’ll step in where regional service teams and partners need deeper expertise, and support installations, commissioning, and repairs when situations require it.

You’ll work directly with leading semiconductor foundries, IDMs, and OSATs, ensuring our systems operate reliably and consistently meet their specifications. You’ll collaborate closely with our Engineering and Applications teams, combining technical problem-solving with a strong customer focus.

This is also an opportunity to help shape our global service function from an early stage, introducing the processes, tools, and standards that will support our growing international installed base.

 

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

 

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

  

What will you do

  • Act as the technical escalation point for regional service teams and distribution partners, resolving issues that require deeper system expertise.

  • Deploy rapidly to customer sites across Europe, the US, and Asia to resolve critical system issues and minimize downtime.

  • Support installation, commissioning, and qualification of our quantum sensing systems when required, working closely with our Munich-based engineering teams.

  • Perform advanced troubleshooting, calibration, and repairs across optical, laser, mechanical, electronic, and software subsystems.

  • Diagnose and resolve complex technical issues systematically, collaborating with Engineering and R&D when root causes go beyond service-level expertise.

  • Work closely with Field Application Engineers, who focus on measurement execution and customer applications, to ensure a seamless customer experience.

  • Support spare-parts planning and service logistics across the global installed base, ensuring critical parts are available for rapid response.

  • Document service activities, technical findings, and root causes, feeding recurring issues and improvement opportunities back into Product Development.

  • Build trusted relationships with customers and partners through clear technical communication and professional service in demanding semiconductor environments.

  • Help establish and continuously improve our global service processes, including escalation workflows, maintenance procedures, troubleshooting guides, and technical documentation.

 

What is expected of you

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in field service, service support, or equipment engineering roles, ideally with semiconductor, optical, laser, inspection, or metrology equipment.

  • A proven track record of resolving escalated or complex system issues that first-line service could not solve.

  • Strong practical troubleshooting skills across complex electromechanical systems, ideally combining optics, lasers, precision mechanics, electronics, and control software.

  • Experience working in semiconductor fabs, cleanrooms, or similarly demanding technical environments, with an understanding of relevant safety and operating procedures.

  • Familiarity with laser safety and interlocked systems, or willingness to complete the necessary technical and safety qualifications.

  • Experience with spare-parts management, service documentation, and ERP or service ticketing systems is an advantage.

  • A structured, independent, and solution-oriented approach to technical challenges, especially under time pressure.

  • Strong communication skills and a customer-focused mindset, with the ability to explain technical issues clearly and build trust with customers, partners, and internal teams.

  • Willingness to travel internationally on a frequent basis, often at short notice, to support customers and partners across the US, Europe, and Asia.

  • Fluency in English. Other languages (e.g. German, Mandarin, Korean) are a plus.

  • A degree in Engineering, Physics, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent technical training and relevant practical experience.

 

Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.

  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.

  • Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.

  • Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.

  • Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 30 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.

  • Learning & development: Your growth is our priority. We provide an annual budget dedicated to courses, conferences, or any resources that help you expand your skills.

  • Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together.

 

About us

QuantumDiamonds GmbH, headquartered in Munich, Germany, develops and manufactures semiconductor inspection systems based on quantum sensing. Spun out of the Technical University of Munich in 2022, the company uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to map electrical current with micrometer precision inside advanced 2.5D and 3D chip architectures. Nine of the world's ten largest semiconductor manufacturers are engaged with QuantumDiamonds, with systems deployed across Europe, the United States, and Asia. The company is investing €152 million to build the world's first production facility for quantum sensing-based semiconductor inspection tools, supported under the European Chips Act.

title: Graduate Applied AI Engineer
descriptionHtml:
TLDR: We’re looking for top 1%, high agency, AI-forward graduates to join the first graduate cohort at Resonance as Applied AI Engineers. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital, to deploy AI into the economy and rebuild businesses for the AI era. You’ll work at the frontier and solve real problems in an environment that champions ownership, autonomy and innovation at pace.

Who we are

Resonance is an applied AI company. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital. Our mission is to close the AI diffusion gap and rebuild businesses for the AI era. We're looking to hire Europe’s elite AI talent.

Why now

We believe the economic diffusion of AI is the major challenge of the next decade. Foundation models are advancing far faster than organisations can absorb them; the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it.

The role

As a Graduate Applied AI Engineer, you’ll build production AI systems for our clients from your first month, working alongside Senior Applied AI Engineers who review your code and coach you. You’ll ship agents, integrations, data pipelines and evals, working across the stack from the AI layer to the client’s core systems and the interfaces people use. You’ll sit with the people who do the work today, see how AI changes it, and help client teams run and extend what we build. You’ll also contribute to Resonance’s own AI products and shared platform, take on more ownership as you grow, and help shape how we train, build and grow as one of our first graduate cohort.

Your first year: Comprehensive training when you join, covering AI engineering, our platform and how we work with clients. You’ll be on a client team from your first month, in a small team where you know everyone by name, founders included. Nobody expects you to know it all when you start: asking for help early is part of the job, and senior people make time for it. You’ll start as a Junior Engineer and typically become an Engineer within 18–24 months.

What we’re looking for: You take the initiative, learn fast and go looking for hard problems. You’re AI-obsessed, trying new models and tools the day they come out. You’re finishing a degree in Computer Science or a closely related subject, such as Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science or Mathematics with a strong programming component, or you graduated in one in the last two years, and you can show what you’re capable of through your grades, competitions, internships, societies or things you’ve built. You write good code in Python or TypeScript and have built something with LLMs: a project, a hackathon entry or an open-source contribution. A software engineering internship, ideally at a startup or fast-moving product team, AI side projects or a company you founded are a plus. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway.

What we offer: Competitive total compensation plus equity. Instead of one product at one company, you’ll ship several production AI systems a year across industries, and help build our own AI products and platform. You’ll learn alongside engineers and operators who have embedded AI into 50+ businesses, in a team aiming to be one of the most talent-dense in Europe and worldwide. Europe is falling behind on AI, and every build moves another European business to the right side of the productivity chasm.

Logistics: London, 3+ days a week in the office or at client sites, mostly in the UK and Europe. English is our working language. We can sponsor visas for eligible candidates. Start date Summer 2027 (dates to be confirmed). We also offer Summer 2027 internships for students in the penultimate year of their degree.

Apply

Send your CV with your grades, your GitHub if you have one, and a short note on something you've built with AI.

We hire people from every background and judge them on what they've built. If you don't tick every box, apply anyway.

Resonance is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. If you need adjustments at any stage, tell us and we'll make them.

title: GTM Engineering Intern | Revenue Operations (d/f/m)
descriptionHtml:
In a nutshell: 4 to 6-month internship in our RevOps team at our Munich headquarters (hybrid), starting between February and April 2027, with the opportunity to move into a full-time role straight afterwards.

About this role at Luminovo

Luminovo builds the B2B SaaS platform that powers the electronics supply chain. DACH is our home market and one of our strongest, and we have recently expanded into North America and the rest of Europe.

GTM engineering at Luminovo is part of Revenue Operations, the department that sits between marketing, sales and customer success and makes sure our revenue organisation runs smoothly.

Our go-to-market engineering function builds the systems that find the right companies and the right people for our sales team: target lists, data enrichment, hyper-personalised outbound campaigns that signal our sellers whom to call next. We work closely with Account Executives, the BDR team and marketing and directly contribute to pipeline generation.

As our GTM engineering intern, you will run outbound campaigns end to end and help build the next layer: signal-based lead generation. You will also help us improve account scoring and build AI automations that take manual work off our sales reps.

There is no textbook for this role. You will learn it the way we did: by building, shipping and seeing what works.

By the end of your internship, you will have shipped revenue systems that our sales & marketing teams rely on every day, and gained hands-on experience in go-to-market engineering, one of the hottest roles on the market right now!

You will also see first-hand how a modern B2B start-up operates day to day, with AI built into its workflows.

This role is for you

  • You combine technical thinking with commercial curiosity: perhaps you studied engineering and want to understand how companies sell, or you have discovered a passion for the commercial side of start-ups.

  • You are keen to work in a fast-paced environment and to grow alongside a high-growth start-up.

  • You bring the drive to learn quickly, a sharp analytical mind and the ambition to take on real responsibility from your first weeks. You collaborate well, ask questions without hesitation and are happy to get your hands dirty.

  • You use AI as more than a better search engine. You have built your own automations, workflows or tools, and can explain what you shipped and what came of it.

  • You are fluent in both German and English. Much of our outbound targets buyers in the DACH region, while the company operates in English.

  • You stand out if you have built something entrepreneurial during your studies, be it a side project, a student society or a small business.

  • You have first experience in GTM engineering, sales operations or automation (this is a big advantage but not a requirement!)

Your performance objectives

🧬 Run outbound campaigns

  • Deliver multichannel campaigns end to end. Build target lists, source and enrich the right contacts, and write the messaging in German and English.

  • Go where coverage is thin. Your campaigns will go wherever our sellers need the most support or wherever there is an opportunity worth pursuing, starting with DACH and extending to the rest of Europe and North America. Take on event campaigns, new regions and opportunistic plays, and turn them around to contribute to our pipeline.

🌀 Build signals and tooling

  • Ship signals. Build plugins or scrapers that generate high-intent leads for our sellers.

  • Process scaling. Transform website engagement into automated outbound triggers and create repeatable playbooks.

⚙️ Build automations

  • Remove manual work. Automate the repetitive manual tasks our revenue teams deal with day to day.

  • Challenge what exists. Get to know the systems we have built, then tell us where they fall short and help improve them.

💶 Unblock the sales team

  • Understand what sales reps need. Work closely with our AEs and BDRs, get to know their accounts and processes, and remove the friction that slows them down.

  • Close the loop. Feed what you learn from replies and campaign results back to sales and marketing.

🗂 Own the data

  • Own enrichment and imports. Take responsibility for account enrichment and every data import into HubSpot on contact, company and lead level.

  • Keep data accuracy high. You will be responsible for maintaining our enrichment so that data stays clean and workflows keep firing.

Your Toolkit

You will learn to work with the most modern sales automation tools on the market, such as Clay, n8n, Twain, Lusha, Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator and many more.

Work location

Our Munich headquarters. For your first two months you will be in the office most days, so you get to know the product, the team, our ICP and the basics of our market. After that, the role is hybrid, with the flexibility to work from home. Occasional travel for team retreats and industry events (expenses covered).

Whom you will be working with

  • Max Hungenbach, Revenue Operations Team Lead and your line manager

  • Danny Bodnar, GTM Engineer, your mentor and day-to-day coach

  • Clifton Lobo, VP Global Sales. You will work directly with him on GTM strategy.

  • Dasha Vyazemskaya, Head of BDR and your partner on handing campaigns over to the BDR team

  • George Knight, Demand Generation Manager in Marketing and your partner on campaigns run alongside marketing

  • Our Account Executives and BDRs across Europe and North America, for whom your campaigns run

Skills, knowledge, and expertise

Just so you know, we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. We care much more about your motivation and ability to help us accelerate technical progress than we care about your CV.

If you’re interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles, see here.

⚡️ About Luminovo

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry.

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress.

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain.

To date, over 300 active customers worldwide are working with us towards this shared goal. Supported by leading investors such as Cherry Ventures, General Catalyst/LaFamiglia, Chalfen Ventures, and others, we have raised more than €20 million.

Our core principles: putting people first & building great things

As a remote-first company headquartered in Munich, our brilliant team is spread across cities including Munich, New York, Austin, Calgary, Berlin, London, Valencia, Nairobi, and Verona, among others. 🌍

Our team includes a mix of product enthusiasts, people advocates, business masterminds, and engineering experts. Among us are graduates from institutions like Stanford University and the University of Cambridge, as well as talented individuals with unconventional CVs. What matters most is their drive to build great things.

We provide an authentic environment based on psychological safety to empower Luminerds from various backgrounds to succeed, grow, and focus on impact. Putting people first means that we deeply care about who our employees are, what makes them unique, and what they excel at.

See what employees and candidates have to say about Luminovo on kununu and Glassdoor.

 

Compensation: €2,650 – €3,150 per month

One year after launch, Kuro runs every day inside the back offices of DACH’s largest construction companies, which together build more than €40 billion a year. We automate their core workflows and help them make faster, better decisions.

As GTM Manager, you'll play a key role in driving Kuro's commercial growth by generating new business opportunities, engaging prospective customers, and turning go-to-market initiatives into results. You are joining Kuro when it matters most. The product is live, our customers are using it daily, but their journey with Kuro has only started, and you can shape it from the get-go. descriptionHtml:
You’ve built data teams from the ground up and know how to turn raw information into better product decisions. You care deeply about how AI is changing software development, and you want to shape the data foundations that make it happen.

Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

JetBrains Air is an AI-native software development platform that connects developer workflows, collaboration, and control into a single system. Because this is a major strategic focus for us, we need a strong data function to help guide it. You’ll own the data strategy for JetBrains AI, partnering closely with product, engineering, and leadership teams to ensure our data infrastructure scales smoothly alongside our ambitions.

Day to day, you will:

  • Uncover insights across the customer journey to improve acquisition, retention, and monetization.

What you’ll need

descriptionHtml:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

As the Head of Talent Acquisition, EMEA, you own the build-out of Anduril's talent acquisition capability across
the EMEA region. Reporting to the Senior Director of Talent Acquisition and partnering closely with the Head of
Strategic Planning for Talent Acquisition, you are a key member of the TA Leadership team with a specific
mandate: geo-specific scaling. You own the in-country, site-specific, and division-specific hiring build-out across
EMEA, working in close partnership with the Head of Talent Acquisition, APAC and with each Divisional Head of
TA who is adding headcount into your region.

This is not a divisional leadership seat. You are not embedded in any single business unit's leadership team; you
are the connective tissue across all of them for one geography. Multiple divisions will be scaling into EMEA at
once, often into the same countries and talent pools, and your job is to make sure their combined demand lands
on a coherent, compliant, and well-resourced regional hiring capability, rather than five uncoordinated efforts
competing for the same candidates.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Regional Strategy and Build-Out
• Define and execute Anduril's EMEA talent acquisition strategy, directly informed by the combined hiring
demand of every division scaling into the region.
• Own EMEA hiring outcomes (time-to-fill, quality, acceptance rates) as the single accountable owner for
regional delivery.
• Own EMEA hiring governance, compliance, and workforce planning across the region's countries, each with
distinct labor law, works council, and candidate market dynamics.
• Develop EMEA hiring playbooks, and partner with the Head of Talent Acquisition, APAC to share what's
working across both regions rather than each building in isolation.
• Partner with the Head of Strategic Planning for Talent Acquisition to evaluate where EMEA needs additional
in-country or sub-regional leadership as demand grows (e.g., a dedicated UK or Germany lead), and help
build the case and the structure for it.

Cross-Divisional Partnership and Prioritization
• Serve as the senior talent advisor to EMEA-based business leaders and to every Divisional Head of TA adding
headcount into the region, synthesizing what could otherwise be five disconnected divisional views into one
coherent regional talent picture.
• Partner with in-region recruiting resources and EMEA business leaders to ensure the regional model reflects
on-the-ground reality, not just headquarters assumptions.
• Act as the tie-breaker when multiple divisions' hiring demand converges on the same country, site, or talent
pool with more need than the region can serve at once, using an objective, business-impact-driven
framework.
• Drive continuous improvement through data and feedback loops, standardizing what should be consistent
across EMEA while preserving the flexibility each country and division genuinely needs.

Operational Cohesion with Peer Regions
• Partner closely with the Head of Strategic Planning for Talent Acquisition, a peer, not a manager, who is
accountable for cross-regional cohesion, shared playbooks, and consistency of operating rhythm across
EMEA and APAC.
• Loop in the Head of Strategic Planning early on build-out choices (tooling, process, governance) so that
EMEA and APAC remain coherent for divisions scaling into both regions.
• Resolve cross-regional alignment issues collaboratively, escalating to the Senior Director of Talent
Acquisition only when peer alignment can't be reached.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
• 10+ years of progressive TA experience, including demonstrated success building or scaling EMEA hiring
specifically, not just supporting it from a distance.
• Deep understanding of EMEA labor markets, employment law, works councils, and compliance
considerations across the region's key countries.
• Proven experience designing and executing an end-to-end regional talent acquisition strategy.
• Demonstrated ability to lead and influence across a matrixed structure, partnering with multiple Divisional
Heads of TA and business leaders who do not report to you.
• Strong track record of driving continuous improvement through data-driven decision making, with the ability
to report regional hiring outcomes credibly to Global TA Leadership.
• Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to reconcile competing divisional demand
for the same regional capacity and drive consensus without formal authority.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

perience partnering with or building out in-country resources as part of a broader regional build.

• Experience building a regional operating model that other regions (e.g., APAC) have adapted or could adapt.

• Prior experience as part of a broader transition from a U.S.-led to a localized, globally scalable TA model.

• Experience in defense, aerospace, or other hardware and software-intensive industries.

• A background in or strong familiarity with BizOps, program management, or business strategy.

Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: 

Benefits

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

    • Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is ----- before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

    • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to
