title: Mechanical Engineer (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
About TACTILIA

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of SCHUNK, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

You design the mechanics of our robotic hands — from the kinematics of a single finger to a complete hand ready for series production.

Multiple drives, gear trains, tendons, tactile sensors and electronics have to fit into a human-sized envelope while surviving hundreds of thousands of cycles. Every millimetre matters, and almost every design decision affects another discipline.

You work hands-on between CAD, test rig and workshop, and report to the CTO.

What you will do:

  • CAD design. Design components, mechanisms and assemblies within tightly constrained envelopes, owning the design from concept through production release.

  • Mechanism & kinematics. Design finger and thumb kinematics, tendon and spindle drives, joints and bearings. Calculate motion envelopes, trajectories, gripping forces and transmission ratios.

  • Calculation & validation. Validate designs through structural and fatigue calculations, FEA, tolerance stack-ups and GD&T before parts are manufactured.

  • Material selection. Select and qualify materials for lightweight structures, wear surfaces, tendons and elastomeric gripping surfaces, and characterise their behaviour under real loads and contact conditions.

  • Assembly design. Design assemblies for efficient assembly, adjustment-free interfaces, serviceability and repair. Specify the required fixtures and tooling.

  • Design for manufacturing. Design for the intended manufacturing process from the outset — machining, injection moulding, sheet metal, additive manufacturing — balancing cost, tolerances and production volumes.

  • Prototyping & testing. Build prototypes, design test rigs and endurance setups, run cycle and load tests, and drive failures to root cause.

  • Documentation & release. Create drawings and BOMs, manage design changes and configuration, and support product development reviews.

  • Suppliers & production. Work with machine shops, material suppliers and manufacturing partners from first prototype through pilot series and production ramp-up.

  • Cross-functional integration. Work closely with Electronics, Sensors and Software to align packaging, interfaces and load paths across the complete system.

What you bring:

  • Degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, precision engineering, or a comparable qualification.

  • 5–10 years of experience in mechanical design of precision mechatronic products, including at least one product taken through to series production.

  • Advanced 3D CAD skills in CATIA, NX, SolidWorks, Creo or comparable systems, with confident 2D drawing creation and GD&T.

  • Strong understanding of mechanism design: linkages, gear trains, bearings, shafts, power transmission, backlash and stiffness.

  • Experience with FEA, structural and fatigue analysis, and tolerance calculations as part of everyday design work.

  • Strong knowledge of material selection for lightweight, high-load and wear-critical components.

  • Practical DFM/DFA experience across multiple manufacturing processes.

  • Hands-on mentality — you build the prototype, run the test and analyse the broken part yourself.

  • Fluent in English and German.

Bonus:

  • Experience with robotic hands, grippers, prosthetics or similarly highly integrated mechanisms.

  • Experience with compact drive trains, including planetary, harmonic or cycloidal gearing, spindle drives and actuator integration.

  • Experience with elastomers, soft goods, injection moulding of complex geometries or compliant structures.

  • Experience integrating tactile or force sensors into mechanical structures.

  • Experience with multi-body simulation or topology optimisation.

  • Knowledge of Machinery Regulation, ISO/TS 15066 and mechanical design for collaborative applications.

The next chapter of robotics won't be built in a lab. It will be built by people who care about what happens when technology meets the real world.

At TACTILIA, you'll work on one of the hardest open problems in robotics: giving machines the dexterity, reliability and robustness to interact with the physical world at industrial scale.

The technology is taking shape, the team is being built, and the standards around robotic hands and their skills are still open. That means your decisions will have a lasting impact — not just on a product, but on what comes next for Physical AI.

Build the hand. Define the standard. Shape what comes next.

If you're excited by the challenge of building robotic hands that works reliably in the real world, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Member of Technical Staff
descriptionHtml:
About Seamflow

Every plane, medical device, lift, battery and building has to be tested, inspected and certified before it reaches the world. It's the invisible layer that keeps the physical economy safe, and it still runs on Word documents, PDFs, spreadsheets and email. Seamflow is the software layer for that industry. We build AI-powered workflows for certification bodies, notified bodies and inspection companies: scheduling and resource planning, technical review, conformity assessment, field inspection, and document intelligence over messy real-world files.

Where we are:

  • Live in production inside some of the largest enterprises in the industry

  • $4.5M seed, 14x oversubscribed, co-led by Northzone and Initialized Capital, the funds behind Spotify, Klarna, Coinbase and Reddit. Angels include Charlie Songhurst and Mario Götze.

  • Demand is outstripping what we can build. That's the reason this role exists.

The team

Most of our engineers were olympiad medallists in maths, physics or informatics before they were engineers. The team has come to us from Google, Amazon, X, Yandex, McKinsey and Bain, and from founding-engineer seats at startups that went on to multi-billion-dollar valuations. We hire against a very high bar, and this role exists to raise it further.

The role

A Product Engineer owns the surfaces people actually work in. A coordinator planning a month of inspections across a fleet of auditors. A reviewer signing off on a technical file. These are dense, stateful workflows where the interface carries real consequences, and where the person using it has done the job for twenty years and will know immediately if the software doesn't understand it.

You own product surface end to end: the interface, the backend that supports it, and the data model underneath. Every customer runs the work differently, so there's no template to fall back on. You decide what the right thing to build is, build it, and are the one who hears about it when it's wrong. You'll ship to production in your first week.

What we're looking for

We care far more about raw engineering strength than about matching a list of technologies. If you're excellent, we'll hire you whether you've spent the last three years in Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, C++ or something we haven't heard of. Our stack is learnable in a fortnight. Judgement, speed and standards are not.

What we're actually screening for:

  • You've built something hard and put it in front of real users. Not a prototype, not a course project. Something that ran, broke, and got fixed.

  • You build genuinely good interfaces, and you can go as deep on the backend as the feature requires.

  • You can hold a complicated workflow in your head and find the version of it that's simple enough to ship.

  • Speed with taste. You ship fast, and you're opinionated about what not to build.

  • You go to the source. You'll read the customer's actual documents, join the actual call, and look at hundreds of real outputs.

Signals we like, none of them required:

founder or ex-founder, founding team experience, early engineer at a startup with a serious engineering culture, EF / YC / Antler, early or stealth-stage startup, design sense you can defend, open source you genuinely maintain.

This is probably not for you if

  • You want a strict boundary between work and life. We run one of the most ambitious startup cultures in Europe: fast paced, extremely high ownership, and in person in Shoreditch.

  • You want a well-defined ticket handed to you each morning.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in your lane.

What you get

  • Real equity, and compensation that reflects a high bar

  • Genuine ownership of product surface area from day one, with the founders in the room

  • Relocation support and visa sponsorship, handled properly

  • Lunch and dinner covered, 24/7 gym access, and any tool that makes you faster

  • A small team with high standards, high trust, and no politics

If this sounds like your kind of problem, apply. A short note on the hardest thing you've built goes further with us than a polished CV.

title: Mid-Level Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

About the role

As a Mid-level Software Engineer at Ledgy, you’ll build reliable, scalable product experiences that help companies manage their equity with confidence. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers, product managers, and designers to turn complex equity workflows into clear, automated, user-friendly software.

This role is a strong fit if you’re ready to take ownership of well-scoped projects, grow your technical judgement, and contribute across the stack while learning from senior peers.

Location: We hire remotely across the UK, Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania. For candidates based in London, we use a hybrid model with 2 days in the office per week.

Teams we are hiring for:

  • Core Equity — Owns the foundational logic that powers Ledgy’s equity engine. Every equity-related event — such as issuing shares, creating new pools, or adjusting ownership — generates transactions. This team defines and maintains the transaction logic, data model, and core domain behaviour that ensure Ledgy’s platform remains accurate, scalable, and compliant. They also enable employees to sell their shares seamlessly once vested.
  • Workflows & Automation — Focuses on automating complex equity workflows and integrating with third-party services, including the trading exchange. The team builds systems that help company admins efficiently onboard and offboard employees, automate equity grants and terminations.
  • Reporting — Transforms Ledgy’s core equity data into financial, operational, and compliance reports. The team manages large, complex datasets and ensures reporting is accurate, performant, and reliable across jurisdictions and company structures. Their work powers the insights companies and auditors rely on for decision-making and transparency.
  • Tax — Ensures taxes are correctly reflected throughout equity operations, especially moments such as exercising, selling, mobility, and other taxable events. As a future team, Tax will build end-to-end product capabilities across the stack, helping customers manage complex tax and compliance requirements accurately across jurisdictions.

You will thrive in the role if you

  • You have 3+ years of experience working as a Software Engineer
  • You are comfortable building and shipping production-quality features across the stack
  • You enjoy learning complex domains and turning them into simple, maintainable product experiences
  • You care about clean, tested, readable code and thoughtful collaboration
  • You are curious about equity, financial workflows, and their real-world impact on companies and employees
  • You’re excited to grow your technical judgement through code reviews, pairing, and architecture discussions
  • You take ownership of your work while asking for input early when trade-offs are unclear

Our Tech Stack*:

We have a modern, cohesive stack that lets us move fast while maintaining quality:

  • Language: TypeScript
  • Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS, tRPC
  • Backend: tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, Temporal
  • Infrastructure: GCP, Terraform Cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, GitHub Actions

*We don’t expect proficiency in this specific stack

What Your Journey Could Look Like

First 30 days:

  • Be paired with an onboarding buddy who will introduce you to the world of equity management
  • Get to know your engineering team, product managers, and designers
  • Learn how your team’s domain connects to the broader Ledgy platform
  • Set up your development environment and start contributing small, well-scoped changes
  • Build familiarity with our codebase, product workflows, and engineering practices

First 3 months:

  • Ship product features and improvements with increasing independence
  • Work with teammates to break down problems, understand trade-offs, and deliver reliable solutions
  • Participate actively in code reviews and team discussions
  • Develop a deeper understanding of how companies manage and automate equity
  • Contribute to improving quality, maintainability, and user experience in your team’s domain

First 6–12 months:

  • Own medium-sized features from implementation through release
  • Collaborate with Product and Design to shape pragmatic, user-centric solutions
  • Contribute to technical discussions around data models, workflows, and scalability
  • Continue growing toward senior-level ownership, judgement, and impact

The interview process:

  • Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role
    • Hackerrank take-home assessment (30-45mins) - this is a test to assess core coding cability
  • Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.
  • System Design (60 min): A system design session focused on practical problem-solving, clear trade-offs, and how you structure technical thinking
  • Behavioural (45 min): Answer behavioural style questions about your experience, using the STAR method - with a PM and EM.
  • Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy’s mission and values
  • Offer 🎉

Being part of Ledgy means:

  • Recharge and re-energize with flexible working hours, 25 days of vacation, and up to 40 days of remote work from outside your home country.
  • We make space for your own professional development, with a generous yearly learning & development budget.
  • This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. All salaries are aligned with competitively benchmarked ranges based on work location and levelling.
  • For candidates based in London or Zurich we use a hybrid work model of 2 days in the office per week.

title: ML Research Intern in Agentic Runtime Systems
descriptionHtml:
Our mission

Constructor’s mission is to enable all educational organisations to provide high-quality digital education to 10x people with 10x efficiency. 

With strong expertise in machine intelligence and data science, Constructor’s all-in-one platform for education and research addresses today’s pressing educational challenges: access inequality, tech clutter, and low engagement of students.

Please send your resume in English only.

Interns are NOT eligible for equipment and other benefits as the position is temporary.

The Reality

The frontier models are converging into commodities; the engine is no longer the differentiator. The scarcity in 2026 is not the model.

We are not looking for people to fine-tune Llama on toy datasets or write "better prompts." We are building the runtime systems that turn probabilistic token generation into reliable workers that finish 50-step tasks without spiraling. We are solving the math of multi-step reliability through engineering, not wishful thinking.

What You Will Solve

You will work on the Agentic Harness, treating the LLM as a component within a larger, deterministic control system. Your research will focus on:

  • Architecting loops that survive error accumulation. You will build verification layers that force the agent to recognize its own hallucinations and self-correct.
  • You will implement systems where the agent compiles its own constraints and the harness enforces them via constrained decoding or external execution.
  • You will optimise KV-cache hit rates and design "restorable compression" strategies to prevent attention decay.

Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for systems thinkers who happen to know ML, not the other way around.

  • You know that a demo is not a product. You are interested in the "boring" engineering: state machines, retries, idempotency, serialisation — that actually makes agents work.
  • You are comfortable working with the raw output of the model and building robust software in Python or Rust around it.
  • You understand why dynamic tool loading destroys inference economics. You prefer deterministic guardrails over "prompting it to be nicer."
  • You are willing to read a 500-line trace of a failed agent loop to find the exact moment the context drifted. You care about the "last mile" of reliability.

What We Offer For Interns:

  • Internship Duration: from 2 months or more 
  • Type of internship:
    • 100% remote
    • or hybrid in the office in Bremen (GER), Sofia (BG), Belgrade (SRB), Istanbul (TR), Sakarya (TR), Singapore (SGD) 

What We Offer

  • 🧠 Patent remuneration
  • 🌴 Paid leave
  • 🧑‍💻 Remote work in locations without our offices
  • Hybrid work in locations with offices (2 days in-office, 3 days remote)

title: Neuroscientist
descriptionHtml:
Type: Full-time
Location: University of Sussex, Brighton - On-site

The Role

Netholabs is building AI grounded in biological intelligence. We record petascale, high-resolution neurobehavioural data from living systems and use it to train neural foundation models — a new substrate for the next generation of AI, robotics, and personalised intelligence. We aim to greatly reduce the burden of animals used in basic scientific research and pharmacological work, with eventual removal and replacement by in silico models.

We're looking for a Neuroscientist to join our Brighton research team as an independent contributor driving experiments from design through analysis. You'll design and run in vivo electrophysiology and behavioural experiments, work with large-scale neural and behavioural datasets, and partner closely with our ML team to translate what we learn about real brains and bodies into better foundation models. This is a role for someone who wants their science to feed directly into what gets built next.

Responsibilities

In Vivo Electrophysiology & Neural Recording

  • Design and run in vivo electrophysiology experiments in animal models

  • Develop and refine neural recording protocols and rigs alongside the hardware team

  • Ensure recordings meet the quality and fidelity standards our models are trained on

Behavioural Neuroscience & Experimental Design

  • Design behavioural paradigms that generate rich, well-controlled datasets

  • Plan and oversee data collection sessions, in collaboration with technicians

  • Iterate on experimental design based on data quality and downstream modelling needs

Data Analysis & Computational Modelling

  • Analyse large-scale neural and behavioural datasets

  • Build and apply computational models to characterise neural and behavioural dynamics

  • Validate findings and communicate results clearly to the broader research team

Neuroscience → AI Translation

  • Partner with the ML team to translate biological findings into model design choices

  • Help define what neurobehavioural data and features are most valuable to capture

  • Contribute to internal research direction connecting neuroscience and foundation model development

Requirements

Core (essential)

  • BSc/MSc in neuroscience, behavioural sciences, or a related field, with hands-on experimental research experience.

  • Preferred: PhD and experience with in vivo electrophysiology and behavioural neuroscience experiments

  • Strong data analysis skills, including experience with Python or a similar language

  • Able to design rigorous experiments and think critically about data quality

  • Excellent communication; comfortable working cross-functionally with engineering and ML teams

Valued (or willing to learn)

  • Experience with large-scale or multi-modal neurobehavioural datasets

  • Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals or foundation model training

  • Experience with computational modelling of neural or behavioural data

  • Prior work bridging neuroscience and AI/robotics research

title: Nordics Marketing Manager
descriptionHtml:
Nordics Marketing Manager

Retire the ERP

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers - automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

Finance deserves better

Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, market or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled.

Light gives them a way out. We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one:

  • Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one.

  • Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting.

  • Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter.

We take on the ERP and the legacy point solution world with something fast to implement, AI-native from the ground up, and better the more you use it.

Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée, and teams across Copenhagen, London and Stockholm, with remotes world over.

The Role

We're looking for a Nordics Marketing Manager to make Light the default finance platform for scaling companies across Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland. You can base yourself in Copenhagen or London.

Light started life in Copenhagen, and the Nordics already know us. Founders, CFOs and finance leaders in the region backed us from the start, and our local community gives us a head start most challengers would envy. Your job is to take that energy to new heights, so that when a Nordic finance team outgrows its current setup, Light is the obvious next move.

You'll own the Nordics marketing plan end to end. You'll have a B-line into our Nordics GTM pod, which spans sales, implementation and customer success, and you'll work closely with our central growth team to find new ways to drive demand through digital channels.

What you'll be doing

  • Building and running the Nordics marketing plan, with pipeline targets you share with the GTM pod.

  • Running a field and events programme across Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo and Helsinki and… any other city you think makes sense. From intimate CFO dinners to flagship moments people talk about for months.

  • Growing partnerships with the accounting firms, advisors, investors and communities that Nordic finance leaders trust and extends our voice across the region.

  • Localising our story, content and campaigns so they land with Nordic finance teams in their own language and context.

  • Creating content with our customers, product and design teams that turns what Light does into stories people want to share.

  • Working with our central growth team to test and scale digital demand generation in the region.

  • Building relationships with local press and the people who shape the Nordic tech and finance conversation.

What we think* you'll need

  • Enough years in the seat to know what works at a fast-growing company, ideally because you've built the ground game for a scaling B2B SaaS business before.

  • A track record across field, events, partnerships and content, and the judgment to know which lever to pull and when.

  • Experience localising a brand and its message for a region, with a feel for what lands with Nordic audiences.

  • Comfort working with sales, implementation and customer success as one team, with pipeline as the shared goal.

  • Deep curiosity about how AI is reshaping finance teams and the companies they serve.

  • A great storyteller across video, text and meme.

  • A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant assholes here, please.

  • Fluency in English and at least one other Nordic language.

  • A passport. Expect regular trips across the Nordics and to our teams in London, Munich, New York and elsewhere.

*If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don't tick every box, we'd still love for you to reach out and convince us you're the right person.

The Good Stuff

  • A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in Copenhagen or London.

  • A competitive salary and potential stock options.

  • 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays in the country where you're based.

  • Regular socials and two company off-sites a year.

  • The chance to shape a category from the inside, in the region where Light began.

Light is an equal opportunity employer.

The Famous Last Words

The Nordics gave Light its first customers, its first champions and its first team. We want to repay that by becoming the finance platform every scaling Nordic company runs on, and we want you to lead the charge. If you know the region, love building from the ground up and want to help retire the ERP for good, let's talk.

title: Onboard Software Engineer - Peripheral Services
descriptionHtml:
Wanna join the adventure?

Loft’s Onboard Software group provides the on-orbit software that powers our satellite fleet — from the Linux services running on the Hub’s onboard computers, to the containerized workloads executing customer applications in low Earth orbit.

The Peripheral Services team owns the software that integrates third-party devices and payloads into Loft’s standardized satellite platform. We enable the control and monitoring of many key spacecraft components, including optical payloads, radios, power controllers, and GNSS receivers. Many of these components are reused across all satellite programs and form the building blocks of our onboard architecture.

The applications developed by our team handle the low-level communication protocol details, exposing the connected devices behind standardized APIs used across mission operations. The team is also responsible for the automation and orchestration that allows Loft to safely and reliably operate the equipment at scale.

In this role, you’ll help develop the software that connects diverse spacecraft hardware to the rest of the platform, and ultimately enables successful missions in orbit.

title: Onboarding Manager
descriptionHtml:
Über Cosuno

Die Baubranche ist eine 14-Billionen-Euro-Industrie, die noch immer auf E-Mails, Excel-Tabellen und eingescannten PDFs läuft. Cosuno ersetzt das durch KI. Generalunternehmer schreiben ihre Projekte auf unserer Plattform an mehr als 250.000 Nachunternehmer aus, und unsere agentische KI findet die passenden Firmen, erkennt Auffälligkeiten in Angeboten und vergleicht jeden Preis mit 6,5 Millionen Datenpunkten aus über 136 Milliarden Euro verarbeitetem Angebotsvolumen. Jede Ausschreibung macht die KI klüger. Die Ergebnisse sind messbar: Generalunternehmer senken ihre Kosten um rund 6 %, Nachunternehmer gewinnen 22 % mehr Volumen, und jeder neue Generalunternehmer-Kunde hat sich in diesem Jahr für unser KI-Produkt entschieden. 2019 in Berlin gegründet und von Cherry Ventures und Spark Capital mit über 40 Millionen Euro finanziert, skalieren wir mit diesem Kapital jetzt Sales, Customer Success und Marketing. Und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

Die Rolle

Du bekommst jede Woche neue Kunden zugewiesen, die sich nicht selbst aktiviert haben, und führst sie durch das Onboarding: Erstkontakt innerhalb weniger Tage, Onboarding-Call per Screenshare, Profil und Suchprofil einrichten, erste Angebote begleiten. Rund 40 Onboardings im Monat, jedes etwa anderthalb Stunden Gesamtaufwand inklusive Vorbereitung und Nachfassen.

Du misst dich nicht am abgehaltenen Call, sondern am Kunden, der danach selbst weitermacht. Dafür verfolgst du die Aktivierungssignale jedes Kunden in Salesforce und greifst nach, wo einer hängen bleibt.

Du bist die Person im Unternehmen, die am häufigsten sieht, wo Neukunden scheitern. Dieses Wissen gibst du strukturiert an Product weiter, damit Tool Tips, Product Tours und Hilfetexte besser werden und mehr Kunden sich selbst aktivieren.

Du berichtest an den Head of Customer Success und arbeitest eng mit dem Sales-Team, das die Kunden abschließt, und mit den Customer Success Managern, die bei Kündigungen übernehmen.

Woran wir dich nach 12 Monaten messen

  • Mindestens 90 % deiner Kunden sind 30 Tage nach dem Onboarding aktiv – Profil vollständig, Suchprofil eingerichtet, erstes Angebot abgegeben.

  • Jeder zugewiesene Kunde hat innerhalb von drei Werktagen von dir gehört.

  • Salesforce ist bei dir vollständig: Onboarding-Status, Aktivierungssignale, Hürden – bei jedem Kunden.

Wer bei Cosuno erfolgreich ist

  • Ownership. Wenn ein Kunde nach 30 Tagen nicht aktiv ist, fragst du zuerst, was du anders hättest machen können.

  • Speed. Du rufst heute an, nicht nächste Woche. Ein Kunde, der drei Wochen wartet, hat Cosuno vergessen.

  • Drive. Du hast schon einmal ein Skript, eine Checkliste oder einen Ablauf gebaut, weil der alte nicht funktioniert hat – ohne dass dich jemand gebeten hat.

  • Low Ego. Du teilst, was bei dir funktioniert, damit das Team besser wird.

Diese Rolle ist für dich, wenn

  • du gern erklärst und dabei merkst, wann dein Gegenüber wirklich verstanden hat – und wann es nur nickt.

  • du 40 Gespräche im Monat als Rhythmus empfindest, nicht als Last.

  • du nach dem dritten Nichterreichen zum vierten Mal anrufst, zu einer anderen Uhrzeit – unsere Kunden stehen auf der Baustelle.

  • du Handwerksbetriebe magst und mit einem Dachdecker genauso sprichst wie mit einer Büroleitung.

Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn

  • du Onboarding als Schulung verstehst und nach dem Call abhakst.

  • du Tickets abarbeiten willst statt Kunden hinterherzutelefonieren

  • du zehn Kunden intensiv betreuen möchtest statt vierzig in die Nutzung zu bringen.

  • dich eine Zahl über deinem Schreibtisch stresst statt motiviert.

Harte Anforderungen

  • Mindestens 1 Jahr in einer kundennahen Rolle mit Volumen: Onboarding, Customer Support mit Aktivierungsziel, Inside Sales, Kundenservice im B2B.

  • Sicher im Erklären von Software per Telefon und Screenshare.

  • Strukturiert und CRM-diszipliniert.

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (C2), Englisch gut.

  • Berlin oder Bereitschaft zu Bürotagen.

Vergütung

55.000 € OTE pro Jahr (Zielgehalt bei 100 % Zielerreichung), bestehend aus einem Fixgehalt und einer variablen Komponente, die sich nach deiner Zielerreichung richtet.

Was wir bieten

  • Klarheit: Eine Zahl, ein Playbook, direkter Einfluss auf dein Ergebnis – und auf das Produkt.

  • Entwicklung: Die Rolle ist der Einstieg in Customer Success bei Cosuno; der nächste Schritt ist Retention Sales oder Produkt-Enablement.

  • Vertrag: Unbefristet, moderne Ausstattung.

  • Arbeitsort: Berlin-Kreuzberg oder hybrid, du wählst.

  • Team: Regelmäßige 1:1s, offene Feedbackkultur, Firmen- und Teamevents.

title: Operational Excellence Manager (Last Mile)
descriptionHtml:
Rohlík Group is one of Europe’s fastest-growing online grocery platforms, changing how people eat and live. Founded in 2014 in the Czech Republic, we’ve grown into a trusted brand with more than one million customers across Czechia, Hungary, Austria, Germany, and Romania.

Our mission is simple to make everyday shopping faster, easier, and more sustainable. We combine smart technology, efficient logistics, and a genuine love for great food. From local bakeries and farmers to our own private labels, we make sure every product that reaches our customers is fresh, safe, and top-quality.

We’re committed to sustainability and supporting local communities, reducing packaging, and working closely with small producers. For our customers, Rohlik Group is more than just shopping, it's a better way to enjoy good food every day.

Department Overview

The Operational Excellence team drives continuous improvement, process standardization, and innovation across Last Mile operations. We support local teams in implementing group standards, solving systemic challenges in routing, loading, and delivery, and enabling sustainable growth as we scale.

 

Role Overview

As Operational Excellence Manager for Last Mile, you will own the design and delivery of a 3 to 6 month continuous improvement roadmap for last mile operations. You will lead adoption of group standards, embed best practices, and deliver sustainable improvements in delivery efficiency, cost per order, and on-time performance. You will partner with central and local stakeholders to find the real bottlenecks in the last mile flow, from route assignment and loading through to the delivery itself, and roll out scalable solutions across sites.

 

What we expect from you

  • Owns the last mile improvement roadmap and makes sure initiatives are delivered on time.

  • Owns initiatives end to end, including group-wide projects: frames the problem, builds and defends the business case, runs the pilot, measures and evaluates the impact, and scales what works across sites.

  • Leads adoption of operational best practices in loading, routing, and delivery through coaching and influence.

  • Partners with group-level development and performance management teams and local site teams to coordinate projects and current performance.

  • Reads the problem in the real operation as well as in the data, tells the true cause apart from the noise, and turns the fix into a standard.

  • Documents processes (VSM, process maps).

 

What we look for

 

Required

  • 5+ years of operational experience owning projects or programs in the last mile for retail.

  • Strong leadership and coaching capability.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management.

  • Analytical thinker who can define metrics, read data, and separate cause from correlation.

  • Project management experience.

  • Willingness to travel 2 to 3 days per week across sites.

 

Preferred

  • Background in e-commerce, grocery, or same-day delivery.

  • Six Sigma and/or project management certification.

 

What’s in it for you

  • Fair reward - You’ll get a strong fixed salary, no bonus games, no politics. Great work is rewarded clearly and fairly.

  • Good food every day - You’ll enjoy a free lunch every day and fresh fruit & veggies in the office. Because good food fuels great work.

  • Life, not just work - You’ll have real flexibility three days in the office, 2 days at the Home Office where it suits you. And unlimited paid vacation based on trust.

  • Personal growth - You’ll grow as fast as Rohlik does. Every challenge is a chance to learn and make an impact.

  • Real impact - What you do here matters. You’ll see your work changing how people eat and live from day one.

  • Recognition among colleagues - Your effort won’t go unnoticed. You can recognise others (and be recognised) through peer credits to use in our internal cafeteria.

  • Xtra membership - You’ll get free Xtra membership and 10% cashback on everything you buy on Rohlik

  • A team that sticks together - You’ll work with people who move fast, support each other and celebrate wins together.

  • If this sounds like you -You’re someone who takes ownership, acts fast and gets things done. Ready to bake something great with us?

title: Operations Administrator
descriptionHtml:

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

title: Operations Intern - Renewable Supply
descriptionHtml:
Operations Intern - Renewable Supply

Festanstellung, Vollzeit · Berlin (HQ)

Unsere Mission für dich

Gestalte mit uns die nachhaltige Energieversorgung von morgen und werde Teil unseres wachsenden Operations-Teams! trawa baut Europas führende B2B-Plattform für saubere Energie auf. Unsere Mission ist es, Industriekunden mit nachhaltigen Energielösungen zu versorgen. Mit einem innovativen Ansatz, der Energieversorgung, fortschrittliche Energiemanagementsoftware und intelligente Optimierung von Energieverbrauchsdiensten kombiniert, helfen wir Unternehmen dabei, erfolgreich zu bleiben und den Weg in eine klimafreundliche Energiezukunft zu ebnen.

Das Team

Du wirst Teil eines kleinen, eingespielten Onboarding-Teams mit vier Personen. Als Teil des Business Operations Departments arbeitest du in einem Bereich mit insgesamt rund 20 Kolleginnen und Kollegen, zu dem auch das Customer Success Team gehört. Im Alltag verbindet uns eine enge, cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit, mit der wir gemeinsam die bestmöglichen Ergebnisse für unsere Kunden erzielen. Wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig, denken mit und packen gemeinsam an. Gleichzeitig pflegen wir eine Teamkultur, die über den Arbeitsalltag hinausgeht – und eine Company Culture, auf die wir wirklich stolz sind.

Als Operations Intern (m/w/d) spielst du eine Schlüsselrolle im Aufbau von Prozessen und Strukturen eines aufstrebenden und schnell wachsenden Technologie-Startups. Wir stellen fortlaufend für eine Praktikumsdauer von 3–6 Monaten ein.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Ownership für operative Prozesse: Du führst entscheidende operative Aufgaben in Eigenverantwortung durch und trägst dazu bei, dass unsere Organisation in allen Kernbereichen reibungslos läuft.

  • Automatisierung von Prozessen: Du entwickelst Ansätze zur Effizienzsteigerung und Automatisierung von Prozessschritten.

  • Begleitung beim Onboarding: Du unterstützt bei der Einführung unserer Neukund:innen in das trawa-Universum und sorgst für eine exzellente Kundenerfahrung.

  • Beitrag zur Weiterentwicklung der Organisation: Du gestaltest Prozesse aktiv mit und hilfst uns dabei, als Unternehmen weiter wachsen zu können.

  • Daten im Blick behalten: Du übernimmst die Datenpflege in unseren Systemen (z. B. CRM) und stellst durch sorgfältige Arbeit eine hohe Datenqualität sicher.

Nach wem wir suchen

  • Du bist Student:in, im Bachelor-Studium, Gap Year, Master-Studium oder Absolvent:in mit guten akademischen Leistungen.

  • Erste praktische Erfahrungen in Startups, anderen schnelllebigen Umfeldern oder der Energiewirtschaft sind ein starkes Plus.

  • Du denkst analytisch, fühlst dich wohl im Analysieren von Zahlen und kommunizierst datenbasierte Erkenntnisse sicher.

  • Organisationstalent zeichnet dich aus – du arbeitest strukturiert, behältst den Überblick und kannst Aufgaben effizient priorisieren.

  • Du besitzt eine generelle Affinität für digitale Tools wie z. B. CRM-Systeme, Notion, Google Workspace oder n8n.

Deine ersten 90 Tage:

Die ersten sechs Wochen – Orientierung und Einarbeitung

  • Lerne unsere Prozesse kennen – vom internen Handover der Neukunden von Sales, über die Anmeldung von Lieferstellen bis hin zur Marktkommunikation im komplexen Energiemarkt.

  • Mache dich mit den wichtigsten Tools, Systemen sowie internen und externen Ansprechpartnern vertraut, die beim Onboarding unserer Neukunden eine Rolle spielen.

  • Führe deine ersten Kunden-Onboardings eigenständig durch: Stelle die „Handover-Readiness" durch Sales sicher, richte das Kundenportal ein, initiiere den Kundenkontakt, melde Lieferstellen an und löse Probleme in der Marktkommunikation.

Bis zum dritten Monat – Verantwortung übernehmen und Prozesse weiterentwickeln

  • Übernimm Kunden-Onboardings eigenständig und verantworte Timelines sowie die Kommunikation mit allen Beteiligten.

  • Entwickle ein belastbares Verständnis für Marktkommunikationsprozesse und werde zur verlässlichen Ansprechperson bei Problemen in deinem Bereich.

  • Erkenne wiederkehrende Muster in typischen Fehlern und bring eigene Ideen ein, um unsere Onboarding-Prozesse gezielt zu verbessern.

Warum wir?

Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der Energiewirtschaft und treibe eigenverantwortlich Projekte voran, die echten Einfluss haben – auf unsere Produkte, unsere Kundinnen und Kunden und die Umwelt. Das erwartet dich bei uns:

  • Dein Impact: Du übernimmst Verantwortung in unserem dynamischen Team und gestaltest aktiv innovative Produkte, die die Energiewende vorantreiben und zur Dekarbonisierung des Mittelstandes beitragen.

  • Flexibles Arbeiten: In unserem schönen Office fördern wir eine lebendige Unternehmenskultur. Homeoffice ist ebenfalls eine Option. Mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, 30 Urlaubstagen und 10 Tagen Workation unterstützen wir deine Work-Life-Balance.

  • Attraktive Benefits: Neben einem wettbewerbsfähigen Gehalt erhältst du Essensgutscheine, eine Urban Sports-Mitgliedschaft, reichlich kostenlose Snacks und ein persönliches Produktivitätsbudget.

  • Persönliche Entwicklung: Du bist Teil eines tollen Teams, wo Coaching und Mentoring groß geschrieben wird, und arbeitest mit Spitzentechnologien und lernst von Branchenexpert:innen.

  • Vielfalt & Inklusion: Bei uns sind alle willkommen – wir engagieren uns für einen integrativen Arbeitsplatz, der Vielfalt wertschätzt. Wir ermutigen Menschen unterschiedlichen Geschlechts, Alters, sexueller Orientierung, ethnischer Zugehörigkeit, sozialer Herkunft und körperlicher oder neurodiverser Vielfalt zur Bewerbung.

Über uns

Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, das grüne Versorgungsunternehmen der Zukunft von Grund auf aufzubauen. Wir schaffen einen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie für B2B-Industrieunternehmen, entwickeln Software und Technologie, um die Volatilität des Energiemarktes zu bewältigen, und professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite.

title: Operations Investigations Graduate
descriptionHtml:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

  • One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

  • Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

  • Profitable since 2017

  • Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs

  • Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot)

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance. We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes.

Join us if you want to

  1. Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

  2. Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

  3. Build the best technology in-house: we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role

This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.

This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role

Some of the areas you'll delve into are:

  • The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.

  • Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.

  • Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.

  • Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.

  • The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.

  • Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.

Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.

No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.

Your team's objectives

Lendable aims to resolve all complaints promptly, ensuring that they are investigated diligently and fairly for customers. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and to reaching the right outcomes for our customers.

Feedback is an important part of how we evolve as a business. The team is encouraged to speak up, take each complaint on its own merits and provide valuable insight back into the business so we can improve and grow.

Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.

What you'll be doing

  • Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits

  • Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards

  • Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised

  • Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale

title: Payroll Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

 

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

 

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

 

About the Role

 

We're hiring a Payroll Specialist to join Sona's payroll bureau, taking hands-on ownership of UK payroll processing for a portfolio of our customers.

Our bureau is growing fast. We're moving from around 15,000 payslips a month to roughly 22,000 by the start of Q4, driven by new customer go-lives in hospitality and care. That means the pace of the role is genuinely high, and we're hiring ahead of that curve rather than catching up after the fact.

Day to day, you'll manage a portfolio of standard and mid-complexity clients across multiple pay frequencies: statutory payments, pension auto-enrolment, HMRC filings and payroll journal reconciliation. You'll also handle client queries through our support desk, working to fast turnaround times. Your work is checked by a Senior Payroll Specialist before it reaches clients, as part of our standard quality process.

This isn't a conventional bureau role. Sona is a startup and the payroll team is still building its own processes and tools, so there's genuine room to shape how things work and to grow as the bureau scales. You'll be working on a product in a sector most software has ignored, and once you're through probation we support CIPP study through the apprenticeship levy.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • Own end-to-end UK payroll processing for a portfolio of Sona customers across multiple pay frequencies, covering standard and mid-complexity clients

  • Manage payroll queries through our support desk, giving clients fast, proactive updates and resolving within SLA

  • Process statutory payments, court orders, standard holiday pay calculations, Alabaster reviews and NMW checks for your own portfolio

  • Handle workplace pension auto-enrolment, contributions, reconciliations and submissions, flagging any miscalculated contributions for investigation

  • Upload, reconcile and submit payments across BACS, Faster Payments and SEPA, and manage payroll journal uploads and reconciliations

  • Manage HMRC filings (FPS, EPS) and year-end processing for your portfolio, escalating disputed or mis-allocated PAYE cases to your Senior or the Payroll Manager

  • Build strong working relationships with clients, including attending client meetings when needed, and flag product bugs to Engineering as you spot them

  • Spot and flag process gaps or improvements within your own portfolio, and support Payroll Assistants and Senior Payroll Specialists with day-to-day queries

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years hands-on experience processing multiple UK payrolls independently

  • Experience within a bureau or outsourced payroll environment is a bonus

  • Good working knowledge of UK payroll and tax compliance, including tax calculations and filing and payment requirements

  • Confident managing a busy queue of support tickets, with strong organisational skills and clear written and verbal communication

  • Comfortable in Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, concatenation) and Google Suite

  • Methodical and accurate under volume, and quick to flag issues rather than let them become problems

  • Bonus: CIPP or equivalent qualification, exposure to Irish payroll (PAYE, PRSI, USC), or confidence using AI tools in your day-to-day work

 

Benefits

 

  • Salary: £35,000 - £45,000

  • Hybrid working - 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho)

  • Share options

  • 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

  • Extra day of leave for every year of service

  • Pension contributions matched up to 5%

  • Comprehensive health insurance

  • Enhanced parental leave & pay

  • Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)

  • Annual all expenses paid team retreats

  • The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

  • Professional development budget

  • Unlimited free books


Note: this represents a typical benefits package for a UK-based, full-time employee. Exact details may vary based on location and employment type but we try to be as fair as possible to all of our team members. Please ask your contact in the Talent team to clarify the available benefits for you.

title: People Operations Specialist
descriptionHtml:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). We’re growing fast! We’re a team of around 200 in 4 locations, and we’re looking for someone to help keep our people processes running smoothly as we scale.

title: Photonic Component Modelling Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Salience Labs is building an industry-defining approach to optical circuit switching for AI infrastructure, engineered for real latency reduction and cost savings. We’re moving towards real-world deployment, and joining at this stage means genuine ownership over that next chapter, working alongside a highly technical team on one of the most consequential problems in AI infrastructure today.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Photonic Component Modelling Engineer to build and qualify behavioral and compact models that accurately capture the underlying device physics. Your models will be the foundation for system-level verification of systems that combine photonic and electronic components.

You’ll need to understand how a component’s behavior shifts with its surrounding optical and electrical circuitry and with operating conditions.

What You’ll Do

Working closely with the system verification, photonic design, and photonic characterization teams, you will:

  • Develop and maintain models of optical primitives (modulators, switches, photodetectors, couplers, etc.) for simulation and system verification environments

  • Verify that models accurately represent device physics across process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners

  • Release models that pass defined QA criteria

  • Verify PDK component libraries so that PDK updates and process variations don’t break circuit-level simulations

  • Extract model parameters from lab measurements and work with characterization to correlate simulation with measurement

  • Build and maintain automated tooling (Python and/or MATLAB) for parameter extraction, model fitting, and regression tracking

  • Maintain regression suites so model and PDK changes are checked against reference data before release

  • Resolve model discrepancies found at system level and feed model-based design risks back to photonic design

  • Keep reproducible records: version-controlled models, scripts, reference data, and QA results

What You Bring

Required

  • MS/PhD (or equivalent experience) in photonics, electrical engineering, applied physics, or a related field

  • 3+ years of experience in photonic component design and/or simulation

  • Solid understanding of integrated photonic building blocks, both passive and active, and their electrical drive requirements

  • Strong scripting ability (Python and/or MATLAB) for model fitting, data analysis, and simulation/measurement correlation

  • Comfortable working in Linux and with version-controlled repositories

  • Strong documentation habits, including model specifications, QA reports, and traceability from reference data to released models

  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach across disciplines

Nice to have

  • Experience modelling signal propagation in photonic integrated circuits

  • Hands-on experience with silicon photonics platforms

  • Experience with optical/photonic simulation tools (e.g., FDTD, mode solvers, circuit-level simulators)

  • Familiarity with foundry PDK-based photonic design flows

  • Tcl scripting

title: Principal Data Engineer, Data Warehouse (TPL)
descriptionHtml:
About Us

Engelhart was founded in 2013 by BTG Pactual Group as a commodities trading company. Our business model is “asset light” and highly diversified – giving us the ability to adapt effectively and nimbly to changing market conditions. We have assembled successful multidisciplinary teams, leveraging advanced fundamental analysis with deep quantitative and weather research capabilities.  Our activities are underpinned by strong risk management practices and by powerful technology and operational excellence. We have exceptional teams with diverse global backgrounds and decades of experience, and are driven by a highly collaborative culture, across products and competencies.

In 2024, Engelhart acquired Trailstone, a global energy trading and technology company. The acquisition provides us with new expertise, analytics and proprietary technology which is being used to provide risk management and optimisation services to help maximise the value of our clients’ renewable power. The acquisition also expanded Engelhart’s capabilities into physical natural gas across North America, a critical fuel to support the energy transition.

Our talented and experienced individuals work together according to its four company values: Performance, Agility, Collaboration, Entrepreneurship.

About the Role 

As Principal Data Engineer, you will own the intraday and end-of-day data serving layer between the CTRM platform and its downstream consumers. You will shape the architecture, standards and engineering practices that enable teams across the business to access trusted, timely and well-defined data. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with the opportunity to influence how the business builds and uses its data platform. 

This will be a full-time role, based in our London office, owning the following responsibilities: 

  • Own the intraday and EOD data serving layer between the CTRM platform and its consumers, including Market Risk, Credit Risk, Treasury, Finance, Reporting and desk tools. 
  • Design and maintain robust data schemas and serving contracts, including SQL, APIs and Kafka-based distribution. 
  • Define data versioning and reproducibility patterns, including as-of timestamps and run IDs, snapshots and incremental updates, with appropriate treatment of position and P&L data. 
  • Own the CTRM-to-warehouse data pipeline, ensuring reliable ingestion, transformation, validation and delivery to downstream consumers. 
  • Lead the implementation and production use of the data warehouse serving layer, closing out the current proof of concept and turning it into a production-ready platform. 
  • Set engineering standards for data modelling, schema evolution, data quality, observability, testing and operational support. 
  • Build and operate solutions using relevant platform technologies, including ClickHouse, S3, Kafka and schema registry tooling. 
  • Work closely with stakeholder teams to understand their needs, propose solutions, explain trade-offs and establish clear, dependable data contracts. 
  • Provide technical leadership to the data engineering team, raising the quality of design and implementation while encouraging collaboration, constructive challenge and continuous improvement. 
  • Help shape the longer-term data architecture and engineering approach as the business and its data requirements evolve.

About You 

You will be a technically strong and proactive data engineering leader who can turn complex business requirements into robust, scalable data products. You are comfortable supporting multiple teams, bringing forward clear recommendations and new ideas, and engaging constructively when your designs are challenged. You want to help shape the future data architecture of the business, not simply deliver against a predefined specification. 

As a result, we believe the following experiences and skills are essential for this role: 

  • Demonstrable experience designing and building data warehouses; this is a non-negotiable requirement. 
  • Hands-on production experience with ClickHouse; this is a non-negotiable requirement. 
  • Experience delivering a columnar OLAP data platform in production, with a strong understanding of analytical query performance and data modelling. 
  • Practical experience with Kafka and event-driven or streaming data architectures.

title: Principal (European Competition practice)
descriptionHtml:
About Charles River Associates

Charles River Associates is a leading global consulting firm that provides economic, financial, and business management expertise to major law firms, corporations and governments around the world. CRA advises clients on economic and financial matters pertaining to litigation and regulatory proceedings, and guides corporations through critical business strategy and performance-related issues. Since 1965, clients have engaged CRA for its combination of industry experience and rigorous, fact-based analysis that provide clients with clear, implementable solutions to complex business concerns.

CRA's European Competition Practice specialises in providing economic advice on matters of competition policy and regulation. We assist firms and their legal advisors in all types of competition proceedings: firms considering merger and acquisition opportunities or involved in merger control proceedings; and firms undergoing investigations relating to cartels, restrictive commercial agreements, abuse of dominance or state aid. We also provide advice to firms involved in regulatory proceedings and sector inquiries. We offer assistance on the estimation of effects and damages in cartel cases, international arbitration and intellectual property disputes.

For more information on the Antitrust and Competition Economics practice in Europe visit http://ecp.crai.com.

Position Overview

Principals have the unique opportunity to learn from, and work alongside, some of the most respected scholars, specialists, and industry experts in the world.  We tailor our analyses to the facts of each case, employing tools such as merger simulation, upward pricing pressure analysis, econometrics, bargaining theory, or game theory as needed. Whether before a court or a regulatory agency, CRA consultants set a high standard for the clear communication of sophisticated economic analysis in complex cases. You will have access to internal training programs focused on creative problem solving, communications, and leading and managing colleagues, teams and cases.  In addition, our firm offers extracurricular activities where you can take additional leadership roles in recruiting, training, and volunteer activities in the local community.

A typical Principal would:

  • Work closely with leading academics and consulting with attorneys and other clients in industry and government on a wide variety of finance, strategy and economics issues;
  • Act as a primary point of contact for clients and assist in the development and presentation of client deliverables including expert reports summarizing our opinions, conclusions, and recommendations and third party financial, market and industry data;
  • Independently conceptualize and identify issues, design complex economic and financial models to analyze economic and financial data;
  • Manage the research process, and supervising, training and mentoring junior analysts;
  • Ensure the integrity and accuracy of analyses and opinions;
  • Work with those testifying in judicial proceedings to provide economic analyses of mergers and other competition matters before the major competition authorities of the world;
  • Assist with recruiting and training of new colleagues.

Desired Qualifications

  • Strong achievement in a graduate degree program (Masters or PhD) with focused study in economics or another quantitative discipline;
  • Extensive and relevant experience (7-11 years), preferably economics/antitrust consulting experience preferred;
  • Demonstrated understanding of economic concepts, competition/regulatory authorities and quantitative and qualitative analysis methods;
  • Exceptional written and oral communication skills;
  • Experience managing and developing teams of junior colleagues;
  • Executive client presence and interaction skills. 

To Apply

To be considered for this position, submit through this job posting:

  • Curriculum Vitae – please include current address, email and telephone number;
  • Covering letter – please describe your interest in a role with CRA's Antitrust and Competition Economics practice in London and how this role matches your goals.  

Work Location Flexibility

CRA creates a work environment that enables our colleagues to benefit from being together in the office to best deliver on our promise of career growth, mentorship and inclusivity. At the same time, we recognize that individuals realize a range of benefits when working from home periodically. We currently expect that individuals spend at least 3 to 4 days a week working in the office (which may include traveling to another CRA office or to client meetings), with specific days determined in coordination with your practice or team.

Responsible AI Use in Recruiting

We believe that recruiting is fundamentally a human process, and we are committed to a hiring process that is consistent, transparent, and people-focused. While AI and other technology-enabled tools help our team operate more efficiently, we strive to provide every candidate with a personalized, thoughtful, and high-touch experience. As CRA invests significant human effort to find qualified members for our teams, we expect candidates to invest corresponding human effort to learn about CRA, prepare thoughtful application materials, and engage with our interviewers. Read more about appropriate hiring manager, recruiting team, and candidate AI at CRA on our website.  

Our Commitment to Diversity

Charles River Associates is an equal opportunity employer (Equality Act 2010). As part of our focus on equity and inclusion, we work to ensure a fair and consistent hiring process. We celebrate diversity and we are committed to an inclusive work environment.

title: Principal Researcher
descriptionHtml:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

About the Team

DoorDash's mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses. At DoorDash, there are three audiences that are at the core of every decision we make - our Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers. The Research team has a direct link to uncover the unmet needs and pain points of each of these audiences. We bring their voices into the business in order to help set the strategic vision for all of DoorDash's current and future products.

About the Role

We're looking for a Principal Researcher to be a strategic research leader for EMEA, shaping what DoorDash builds next. You'll combine deep expertise in qualitative and quantitative methods to find the unmet needs, behavioral shifts, and market openings that point to new products and new growth. You'll work as a peer to senior product, design, engineering, data science, and business leaders, and your work will directly inform roadmaps, investment decisions, and company-level strategy.

This role is built for a seasoned researcher who is equally comfortable in a living room interview, a survey dataset, and a leadership review, and who uses AI as a daily tool to move faster and see further, without giving up the judgment that makes research trustworthy. You'll also raise the bar for the wider research practice by mentoring researchers, sharing methods, and helping the team define what great looks like in an AI-enabled era.

What You'll Be Doing

Shape Product Strategy: Translate deep understanding of Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers into a clear point of view on where DoorDash should play and win. You'll frame the highest-stakes questions, bring evidence to roadmap and investment debates, and influence decisions at the director and executive level.

Detect New Opportunities: Proactively identify emerging needs, behavior changes, and white space that point to new products, new verticals, and new growth levers. You'll size and validate opportunities with a mix of foundational discovery, market and competitive context, and behavioral data, and turn them into concepts teams can act on.

Lead Mixed-Methods Research: Design and run rigorous research end to end, choosing the right method for the question: ethnography, in-depth interviews, diary studies, and usability testing alongside surveys, conjoint and MaxDiff, segmentation, experiment design, and behavioral and log analysis. You'll triangulate across sources so the "what," the "how much," and the "why" tell one coherent story.

Partner with Data Science and Experimentation: Work closely with data science and analytics to connect qualitative insight to A/B test design, metrics, and product outcomes, and to explain the "why" behind results. You'll help teams learn from what worked, what didn't, and what to test next.

Apply AI to the Research Craft: Use AI tools and LLMs in your daily workflow for synthesis, analysis, survey and discussion guide design, and scaling qualitative depth, and design human-in-the-loop checks that catch confident but wrong outputs. You'll help the team identify where AI accelerates research and where it should not be trusted, and contribute to shared prompts, workflows, and standards. You'll also study how people experience AI-powered features across DoorDash's products.

Influence and Communicate: Tell compelling, decision-ready stories that move partners from insight to action. You'll adapt depth and format to the moment, from a fast directional read that unblocks a team this week to a foundational body of work that anchors a multi-year strategy, and you'll follow through to see that findings change what gets built.

Lead Through Others: Serve as a thought partner and mentor to researchers across levels, review and elevate research quality, and help partners run good research on their own where that makes sense. You'll help set the team's research agenda, methods, and standards, and contribute to hiring and growing the team.

Operate Across Brands and Regions: Bring a global lens to your work, partnering across brands, markets, and cultures and adapting approaches to local context so that insights scale beyond a single market.

What We're Looking For

  • 10+ years of experience in user, market, or product research at a technology company (or equivalent depth), with a track record of leading ambiguous, high-visibility work at staff level or above
  • Demonstrated impact on product strategy: examples where your research changed a roadmap, unlocked a new product or line of business, or redirected significant investment
  • Proven ability to detect and shape new product or growth opportunities, from early signal through validated concept
  • Expert command of both qualitative and quantitative methods, including interviews, ethnography, and usability testing as well as survey design, statistical analysis, and experimentation. Working knowledge of SQL, R, or Python for pulling and analyzing your own data is a plus
  • Hands-on experience using AI and LLMs in research (for example, synthesis, analysis, prototyping, or scaling qualitative work), with sound instincts about where they help and where they mislead. Experience researching AI-powered products is a plus
  • Experience in consumer, two-sided or multi-sided marketplace, logistics, commerce, or local services contexts is a plus
  • Exceptional storytelling and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders without authority and build trust across product, design, engineering, data science, and business teams
  • A bias for speed and pragmatism: comfortable delivering directional insight quickly while knowing when a decision calls for deeper rigor
  • Experience mentoring or coaching researchers and raising the quality of a research practice

title: Principal Software Engineer - Real-Time Voice
descriptionHtml:
About Parloa

Parloa's mission is to make every customer conversation feel effortless for both customers and the companies serving them. About The Role:

Voice is one of the most demanding and differentiated parts of what we do. As Principal Software Engineer for Voice/VoIP, you'll own the technical direction of our real-time voice infrastructure — the systems that let AI agents have natural, low-latency phone conversations at enterprise scale, across telephony providers, carriers, and global markets.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You'll set architectural direction, solve the hardest problems yourself, and raise the bar for how the wider engineering org builds and reasons about voice systems. You'll work closely with infrastructure, AI/ML, and product teams to ensure our voice stack is fast, reliable, and ready to scale globally.

Areas Of Ownership:

  • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for Parloa's Voice/VoIP infrastructure, including SIP trunking, media handling, and real-time audio pipelines

  • Design for low-latency, high-availability voice at enterprise scale — across global telephony carriers and providers

  • Drive technical decisions on protocols and standards (SIP, SDP, RTP/SRTP, RTCP, WebRTC, ICE, STUN/TURN) and real-time media transport

  • Partner with AI/ML teams to optimise the integration between voice infrastructure and conversational AI models (ASR, TTS, turn-taking, barge-in)

  • Diagnose and resolve deep, systemic issues in call quality, latency, jitter, and packet loss across distributed, multi-region deployments

  • Define and uphold engineering standards for reliability, observability, and security across the voice stack

  • Mentor senior and staff engineers, acting as a technical multiplier across the organisation

  • Strong knowledge of SIP, SDP, RTP/SRTP, RTCP, WebRTC, ICE, and real-time media transport protocols

  • Hands-on understanding of audio codecs and media behavior, including Opus, G.711/G.722, codec negotiation/transcoding, DTMF/RFC2833, jitter buffers, packetization, and codec-related quality/latency trade-offs

  • Excellent communication skills — able to explain complex technical trade-offs to engineers and non-engineers alike

  • A genuine interest in AI and conversational technology, and how voice infrastructure underpins it

When millions of people reach out to a brand, those interactions aren't just support tickets; they're defining experiences. We're here to raise the standard: making every conversation seamless, intelligent, and genuinely helpful. If you care about shaping how businesses and customers connect at scale and want your work to matter in real, everyday moments, this is where you do it.
